definition_zh: 充实；使丰富；提高价值或品质
definition_en: to improve the quality or value of something, or to add interesting material to it
core_image: 往一杯清水里加入果汁与果肉，平淡的液体立刻有了滋味与颜色
scene: 她把同学们的反馈逐条吸收进方案，让报告更充实。New feedback enriched the final report.
sceneCN: 这里 enrich 是「充实；使丰富」（第 1 个义项：提高品质或价值）；句意：新的反馈使最终报告更加充实。

senses.title: To raise the quality or value of something
senses.definition: to add something that makes a thing better, more interesting, or more useful
senses.definitionCN: 加入某些内容，使事物更好、更有趣或更有用
senses.example: Field trips enrich science lessons.
senses.exampleCN: 实地考察让科学课更加丰富。
senses.why: The prefix en- means to make, so the verb turns richness into something you give to another thing.
senses.whyCN: 前缀 en- 表示「使成为」，因此这个动词把「丰富」变成你赋予他物的东西。

senses.title: To make land or food more nutritious
senses.definition: to add nutrients or valuable substances to soil, water, or food
senses.definitionCN: 向土壤、水源或食物中添加养分或有用物质
senses.example: Farmers enrich the field with compost.
senses.exampleCN: 农民用堆肥给田地增肥。
senses.why: The same idea of adding worth applies literally to soil, where what is added is nutrient rather than interest.
senses.whyCN: 同样的「添加价值」义项可本义用于土壤，只是所添加的是养分而非趣味。

senses.title: To increase the wealth of a person or group
senses.definition: to give someone or a group a great deal of money or resources
senses.definitionCN: 使某人或某群体拥有大量金钱或资源
senses.example: The oil boom enriched a whole region.
senses.exampleCN: 石油热潮使整个地区变得富裕。
senses.why: Extended from material value to money, the verb can name the process that makes people financially rich.
senses.whyCN: 从物质价值延伸到金钱，这个动词可指使人变富的过程。

intro.en: Enrich pairs the prefix en- with rich, an adjective that English already had before the verb was built.
intro.cn: enrich 由前缀 en- 与 rich 组成；英语先有这个形容词，之后才造出动词。

items.en: Rice meant powerful or good, the ancestor of rich.
items.cn: rīce 意为强大的、优良的，是 rich 的前身。

items.en: The prefix en- was used to build verbs meaning to make something so.
items.cn: 前缀 en- 用来构成「使成为某种状态」的动词。

items.en: enricher appears in administrative records of England.
items.cn: enricher 出现在英国的行政文书中。

items.en: The verb spreads in the sense of making people wealthy.
items.cn: 该动词在「使人致富」义项上普及开来。

items.en: Abstract uses such as enriching experience become standard.
items.cn: 充实经验这类抽象用法成为现代表达。

note.en: Group one holds family words built on the same verb; group two holds other verbs of adding value.
note.cn: 第一组是同一动词派生的同族词；第二组是其他表示增添价值的动词。

entries.definition: The action or result noun of the verb, common in mining and in education programmes.
entries.definitionCN: 该动词的动作或结果名词，常见于矿业与教育项目。

entries.definition: A person or machine that adds value; in water treatment it names the dosing unit.
entries.definitionCN: 指人或设备；在水处理中指添加装置。

entries.definition: The adjective that supplies the meaning; the prefix only turns it into an action.
entries.definitionCN: 提供核心义的形容词；前缀只把它变成动作。

entries.definition: Built the same way from dear, but the result is affection rather than abundance.
entries.definitionCN: 同样由 dear 加前缀构成，但结果是喜爱而非充裕。

entries.definition: To improve the appearance or value of something already good; less about adding new material.
entries.definitionCN: 提升本已不错之物的外观或价值，较少强调增添新内容。

entries.definition: To make stronger, often with added nutrients in food or drink.
entries.definitionCN: 使更强，常指在食物饮料中加入营养成分。

entries.definition: To supply what a living thing needs to grow; the biological side of adding value.
entries.definitionCN: 供给生长所需，是增添价值的生物层面。

entries.definition: To add decoration, sometimes to a story, so the gain may be ornamental rather than real.
entries.definitionCN: 添加装饰，有时用于故事，因此增益可能只是装饰性的。

normalIntro.en: Enrich contains rich, so the whole verb can be read as making something rich.
normalIntro.cn: enrich 内含 rich，因此整个动词可读作「使变得富有」。

normal.en: En- means to make, so enrich means to make rich.
normal.cn: en- 表示使，所以 enrich 就是使富有。

normal.en: Pair it with soil, curriculum, and life, the three things exams mention most.
normal.cn: 把它与土壤、课程、生活搭配，这是考试最常提的三个对象。

normal.en: Use enriched for the result and enriching for the activity itself.
normal.cn: enriched 表结果，enriching 表活动本身。

normal.en: Do not confuse it with enrich oneself, which stresses money rather than quality.
normal.cn: 不要与「致富」混淆，后者强调金钱而非品质。

normal.en: In writing, enrich replaces add value to with one verb.
normal.cn: 写作中，enrich 可一词替代 add value to。

abstract.en: Picture a plain bowl into which someone keeps pouring colorful fruit.
abstract.cn: 想象一只素碗，不断有人往里倒入彩色果肉。

abstract.en: Imagine a farmer turning dark compost into tired soil.
abstract.cn: 想象农夫把堆肥翻进疲惫的土地。

abstract.en: Think of a vault filling coin by coin until the door barely closes.
abstract.cn: 想象金库一枚枚堆币，直到库门将合不拢。

examples.en: Reading widely enriches your writing.
examples.cn: 广泛阅读会让你的写作更有内涵。

examples.en: The programme was enriched with local case studies.
examples.cn: 该项目加入了本地案例研究。

examples.en: Nothing enriches a city like a good library.
examples.cn: 没有什么比一座好图书馆更能充实一座城市。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因 rich」——因为想要 rich，所以去 enrich；这只是拆词联想，与词源无关。

root: 古英语 rīce（强盛的）→ rich＋古法语前缀 en-（使成为）→ 盎格鲁-诺曼语 enricher → 中古英语 enrichen → 现代英语 enrich，核心义「使变得丰足」。

sensesIntro.en: The verb starts with adding worth to a thing, moves to feeding soil and food, and ends with making people wealthy.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个动词从为事物增添价值出发，转到为土壤与食物添加养分，最后落到使人富裕。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: something poured into a plain container until it overflows with value.
core.cn: 核心意象：不断往素器里注入东西，直到价值满溢。

branches.en: Adding worth to lessons and texts is the abstract core.
branches.cn: 为课程与文本增添价值，是抽象的核心用法。

branches.en: Feeding soil keeps the idea physical and agricultural.
branches.cn: 给土地施肥，让这个概念保持在农业实物层面。

branches.en: Money extends abundance to people and regions.
branches.cn: 金钱把充裕延伸到人与地区。

branches.en: Both senses describe adding something that was missing.
branches.cn: 两个义项都在说补入原本缺少之物。

branches.en: Fertile land and mineral wealth both turn into riches.
branches.cn: 肥沃土地与矿藏财富都会转化为财富。

intro.en: Enrich is a native verb with a French prefix, and its small family grows with English endings.
intro.cn: enrich 是带法语前缀的本族动词，其词族靠英语词尾扩展。

latinIntro.en: Latin divitis means wealthy and was used by scholars who translated the verb into legal Latin.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 divitis 表示富裕，曾被把该动词转译为法律拉丁语的学者使用。

items.example: En- turns rich into a verb.
items.exampleCN: en- 把 rich 变成动词。

items.example: The old form is the source of modern rich.
items.exampleCN: 古形是现代 rich 的来源。

items.example: Uranium enrichment is a technical phrase.
items.exampleCN: 铀浓缩是一个技术短语。

items.meaning: a person or device that adds value
items.example: A soil enricher is sold in garden shops.
items.exampleCN: 土壤改良剂在花店有售。

items.example: It is the opposite of enrich.
items.exampleCN: 它是 enrich 的反义词。

definition_zh: 注册；报名；招收；登记加入
definition_en: to put a name, one's own or another's, on an official list in order to join a course, school, organization or program
core_image: 一支笔在羊皮卷轴的名字栏上落下，卷轴一圈圈卷起，刚写的名字被卷进册子里
scene: 注册台前，一名学生把填好的表格递过去，工作人员在卷起来的册子上找到空行，笔尖悬着等他确认。She enrolled in a night course on statistics.
sceneCN: 这里指「为自己报名课程」（第 1 个义项：把本人姓名登记进课程名册）；句意为她报名参加了一门统计学夜间课程。图中可辨识物件：表格、卷起的册子、签字笔、注册台。

senses.title: To register oneself for a course
senses.definition: to add one's own name to the list for a class or program
senses.definitionCN: 把自己的名字加入某门课程或项目的名册
senses.example: She enrolled in a night course on statistics.
senses.exampleCN: 她报名参加了一门统计学夜间课程。
senses.why: the verb keeps the physical image: a name is written onto a roll, and the writer is the one who benefits.
senses.whyCN: 动词保留具体意象：把名字写进卷册，而写名字的人正是受益者。

senses.title: To take students in
senses.titleCN: 招收学生（机构主动收录）
senses.definition: to admit and record students as an institution
senses.definitionCN: 作为机构录取并登记学生
senses.example: The college enrolls about four hundred students each year.
senses.exampleCN: 这所学院每年招收约四百名学生。
senses.why: the same verb is used from the institution's side, where the hand holding the pen is not the student's.
senses.whyCN: 同一个动词从机构一侧使用，握笔的手不是学生的。

senses.title: To join an organization
senses.definition: to sign up as a member of a union, party, club or similar body
senses.definitionCN: 报名成为工会、政党、俱乐部等团体的成员
senses.example: He enrolled in the union during his first week on the job.
senses.exampleCN: 他在上班第一周就加入了工会。
senses.why: once the list is no longer a school roll, the verb simply means joining any body that keeps members.
senses.whyCN: 当名册不再是学生册，动词就泛指加入任何保存成员名单的团体。

senses.title: To register another person
senses.definition: to enter someone else's name, as a parent does for a child
senses.definitionCN: 把别人的名字登记进去，如家长替孩子办理
senses.example: Parents must enroll each child before the term starts.
senses.exampleCN: 家长必须在开学前为每个孩子办理注册。
senses.why: English allows the verb to take a person as its object, so the writer and the person named can differ.
senses.whyCN: 英语允许这个动词以人为宾语，因此写名字的人与被登记的人可以不同。

senses.title: To sign up for an event
senses.definition: to put a name down for a trip, contest or one-off event
senses.definitionCN: 为出行、比赛或一次性活动登记名字
senses.example: Dozens enrolled for the field trip before the notice went out.
senses.exampleCN: 通知发出前就有几十人报名参加了野外考察。
senses.why: the list need not be permanent; a single sheet by the door is enough to make the verb apply.
senses.whyCN: 名册不必长期存在；门口一张单子就足以让这个动词成立。

senses.title: To join a benefit plan
senses.titleCN: 加入保险或福利计划（美式）
senses.definition: to sign up for health cover, insurance or a savings scheme during an open period
senses.definitionCN: 在开放期内加入医疗保险、保险或储蓄计划
senses.example: Employees may enroll in the health plan every November.
senses.exampleCN: 员工每年十一月可以加入医疗计划。
senses.why: American administrative usage applies the list image to benefits, where the roll is held by an employer or insurer.
senses.whyCN: 美式行政用语把名册意象用到福利上，名册由雇主或保险方保管。

senses.title: To include something in a scheme
senses.titleCN: 把某物正式纳入计划或体系
senses.definition: to bring a place, asset or activity formally into a program
senses.definitionCN: 把地点、资产或活动正式纳入某项计划
senses.example: The agency enrolled the wetland in a restoration scheme.
senses.exampleCN: 该机构把这片湿地纳入了修复计划。
senses.why: the object widened from people to things once the list became a register of protected assets.
senses.whyCN: 当名册变成受保护资产的登记表，宾语就从人扩展到物。

senses.title: To register for credit
senses.titleCN: 正式注册修读（与旁听相对）
senses.definition: to register in a course so as to receive credit, rather than attend as a visitor
senses.definitionCN: 注册修读课程以取得学分，而非以旁听身份到场
senses.example: He enrolled for credit instead of sitting in as a visitor.
senses.exampleCN: 他正式注册修读，而不是以访客身份旁听。
senses.why: school offices needed a verb that separated the recorded student from the casual attender.
senses.whyCN: 学校教务需要一个动词，把在册学生与偶尔到场者区分开。

intro.en: Enroll comes from Old French enroller, built on rolle 'roll, list', which goes back to Latin rotulus 'little roll'.
intro.cn: enroll 来自古法语 enroller，由 rolle「卷册、名单」构成，后者上溯拉丁 rotulus「小卷轴」。

items.en: A rotulus was a small scroll; names of citizens, soldiers or students could be written on one.
items.cn: rotulus 指小卷轴；公民、士兵或学生的名字都可以写在上面。

items.en: Old French rolle named such a scroll, and the verb enroller meant to write a name onto it.
items.cn: 古法语 rolle 指这种卷册，动词 enroller 意为把名字写到上面。

items.en: English took the verb in the fourteenth century, first for entering names on an official register.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪引入这个动词，最初指把名字写进正式登记簿。

items.en: By the sixteenth century the verb was applied to matriculation, and the school sense became dominant.
items.cn: 到十六世纪，这个动词已用于入学登记，学校义逐渐占据主导。

items.en: In twentieth-century American administration the verb extended to insurance and savings plans.
items.cn: 在二十世纪的美国行政语境里，这个动词扩展到保险与储蓄计划。

items.en: Dating note: the fourteenth-century first citation is approximate, and the exact route from 'scroll' to 'school register' is generally accepted rather than documented step by step.
items.cn: 年代说明：十四世纪的最早书证只是约数；从「卷轴」到「学生名册」的路径一般认为是自然引申，但没有逐环文献记录。

note.en: Group one holds spellings and relatives of the same verb; group two holds other verbs of joining.
note.cn: 第一组是同一动词的拼写与同族形式；第二组是其他表示加入的动词。

entries.definition: The British spelling, with a single l; the past forms also double the l in British usage.
entries.definitionCN: 英式拼写，只保留一个重复的辅音字母；英式过去式也把这个字母写两遍。

entries.definition: The noun of action; the verb names the deed, the noun names the deed and its count.
entries.definitionCN: 动作名词；动词指行为，名词兼指行为与人数。

entries.definition: A person who has been enrolled; the ending marks the one affected by the action.
entries.definitionCN: 被登记的人；词尾标记动作的承受者。

entries.definition: Built on the same roll but with a prefix meaning 'out': to open a scroll rather than write on it.
entries.definitionCN: 同样以「卷」为词干，但前缀表示「向外」：把卷轴展开，而非在上面书写。

entries.definition: To record formally in a register; it is the general verb, while enroll keeps the school and membership flavour.
entries.definitionCN: 在登记簿上正式记录；它是通用动词，而该词保留学校与会员的色彩。

entries.definition: The everyday phrase for putting your name down; enroll is its formal counterpart.
entries.definitionCN: 把名字写下的日常说法；该词是其正式对应词。

entries.definition: To be formally admitted to a university register; narrower and more ceremonial than enroll.
entries.definitionCN: 正式被录入大学名册；比该词更窄、更具仪式性。

entries.definition: To join the armed forces or recruit someone for a cause; the list here is a military muster.
entries.definitionCN: 参军或为某项事业招募；这里的名册是军队的花名册。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphology, real fixed phrases and real office scenes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实构词、真实搭配与真实的办事窗口场景。

normal.en: A prefix meaning 'in' plus roll, the scroll of names: to write a name inside the roll.
normal.cn: 表示「进入」的前缀加指卷册的名词：把名字写进卷册里。

normal.en: The noun adds an ending for the act, and the person affected takes a short ending of their own.
normal.cn: 名词加表示动作的词尾，受影响的人则另加一个短词尾。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: enroll in a course, enroll at a university, enroll new members.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：报名课程、在某大学注册、吸纳新成员。

normal.en: British usage writes a single l, American usage doubles it.
normal.cn: 英式只保留一个重复的辅音字母，美式则把这个字母写两遍。

normal.en: The same family covers the register, the registrar's act and the person on the list.
normal.cn: 同一词族覆盖名册、登记动作与名册上的人。

abstract.en: Picture a name being rolled into a scroll so it cannot fall out.
abstract.cn: 想象一个名字被卷进卷轴，再也掉不出来。

abstract.en: Picture a turnstile that clicks once per name written.
abstract.cn: 想象一道闸机，每写下一个名字就响一声。

abstract.en: Picture a seed pressed into soil: joining is the pressing, growing comes later.
abstract.cn: 想象种子被按进土里：加入只是按下，生长是后来的事。

examples.en: She enrolled in a night course on statistics.
examples.cn: 她报名参加了一门统计学夜间课程。

examples.en: The college enrolls about four hundred students each year.
examples.cn: 这所学院每年招收约四百名学生。

examples.en: Employees may enroll in the health plan every November.
examples.cn: 员工每年十一月可以加入医疗计划。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「入」加「卷册」：把名字写进名册 → 注册、招收

root: 古法语 enroller「把名字写入卷册」，由 rolle「卷册」加表示「进入」的前缀构成；rolle 上溯拉丁 rotulus「小卷轴」，其为 rota「轮子」的指小形式。

sensesIntro.en: The eight senses all describe one hand writing a name, viewed from the writer, the institution, the organization, the parent, the event sheet, the benefit plan, the protected asset and the credit register.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都描述同一只手写下名字，只是分别从本人、机构、团体、家长、活动单、福利计划、受保护资产与学分名册的角度看。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a pen touching the name line of a scroll that is being rolled shut.
core.cn: 核心意象：笔尖落在卷轴的名字栏上，卷轴正被卷起。

branches.en: SELF AND CREDIT: the student writing his own name, once for interest and once for a record.
branches.cn: 本人与学分：学生写下自己的名字，一次为兴趣，一次为记录。

branches.en: TAKING IN AND EVENT SHEETS: the institution's hand, and the single sheet by the door.
branches.cn: 收录与活动单：机构的手，以及门口那张一次性的单子。

branches.en: MEMBERS AND CHILDREN: joining a body, and writing a name on someone else's behalf.
branches.cn: 成员与孩子：加入团体，以及替别人写下名字。

branches.en: BENEFIT ROLL: the same act inside an employer's plan.
branches.cn: 福利名册：同一动作发生在雇主的计划里。

branches.en: ASSETS ON A REGISTER: the object widened from people to places and things.
branches.cn: 登记在册的资产：宾语从人扩展到地点与物。

intro.en: Enroll is a prefix on a base that came from Latin through French, and the same pieces build the noun, the British spelling and the person registered.
intro.cn: 这个词是前缀加一个经法语来自拉丁的词干，同样的部件还构成名词、英式拼写与注册者名称。

latinIntro.en: Latin rotulus 'little roll' gives roll and enroll; rota 'wheel' is the older word behind it.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 rotulus「小卷轴」衍生出 roll 与 enroll；更早的词是表示「轮子」的 rota。

items.example: The prefix puts the name inside the roll.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把名字放进卷册里。

items.structure: roll (base word, from Latin rotulus 'little roll')
items.example: The clerk read from the roll.

items.meaning: to write a name onto a list
the act or count of registering
items.example: Enrollment rose after the fee cut.
items.exampleCN: 降费之后注册人数上升。

items.meaning: the same noun in British usage
items.meaningCN: 英式拼写下的同一名词
items.example: Enrolment figures are published each term.
items.exampleCN: 英式拼写下的注册数据每学期公布。

items.example: Every enrollee gets a lab card.
items.exampleCN: 每位注册者都领到实验卡。

items.meaning: to take a name off the list

items.example: Adults can re-enroll after a break.
items.exampleCN: 中断之后成人可以重新注册。

definition_zh: 注册；入学登记；登记人数
definition_en: the act of adding a name to an official list, or the number of names on that list
core_image: 新生排队把名字写进一本厚厚的登记簿，写完一页再翻下一页
scene: 九月初教务处的窗口前排起长队，大家都在办理注册。Enrolment closes at the end of September.
sceneCN: 这里 enrolment 是「注册；入学登记」（第 1 个义项：把姓名登入正式名单的行为）；句意：九月底结束注册。

pos.zh: 注册；入学登记；登记人数

derivatives.zh: 登记入册；招收（英式拼写）

senses.title: The act of joining an official list
senses.definition: the process of putting your name on the list of a school, course, or organisation
senses.definitionCN: 把姓名列入学校、课程或机构名单的过程
senses.example: Enrolment takes about ten minutes online.
senses.exampleCN: 在线注册大约需要十分钟。
senses.why: The noun is built on the verb for writing a name on a roll, so the action keeps that bookkeeping image.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词造自「把名字写进名册」的动词，因此保留了登记簿的画面。

senses.title: The number of people registered
senses.definition: the total number of people who have joined an institution in a given period
senses.definitionCN: 某段时期内加入某机构的总人数
senses.example: University enrolment rose sharply last year.
senses.exampleCN: 去年大学入学人数大幅上升。
senses.why: Because lists are counted, the word shifts from the act to the size of the list it produces.
senses.whyCN: 名单可以被清点，于是词义从行为转向该行为产生的名单规模。

senses.title: The state of being a member of a scheme
senses.definition: the fact of being officially registered in a programme or benefit scheme
senses.definitionCN: 正式登记参加某项目或福利计划的状态
senses.example: Enrolment in the pension scheme is voluntary.
senses.exampleCN: 养老金计划的参加是自愿的。
senses.why: Extended to schemes, the noun names an ongoing status rather than a single act at a desk.
senses.whyCN: 延伸到各类计划后，这个名词指的是一种持续状态，而非柜台前的一次动作。

intro.en: Enrolment comes from the verb phrase meaning to put a name on a roll, a rolled-up paper list.
intro.cn: enrolment 来自「把名字写上卷起的名册」这一动词短语，roll 原指卷起来的纸名单。

items.en: Rotulus means a little roll of paper used for lists.
items.cn: rotulus 指用来登记名单的小纸卷。

items.en: Rolle means the list itself, and enroller means to enter on it.
items.cn: rolle 指名单本身，enroller 指登记其上。

items.en: The verb enren appears in tax and household records.
items.cn: 中古英语出现 enren，用于税务与家事记录。

items.en: Enrol with the doubled consonant becomes standard in legal use.
items.cn: 近古英语中，双写辅音的 enrol 成为法律用法。

items.en: The noun splits into British enrolment and American enrollment.
items.cn: 现代英语中该名词分出英式 enrolment 与美式 enrollment。

note.en: Group one holds the verb family and spelling variants; group two holds other words for signing in.
note.cn: 第一组是动词同族与拼写变体；第二组是其他表示登记的词。

entries.definition: The British verb behind the noun; the American verb writes a second letter.
entries.definitionCN: 该名词背后的英式动词；美式动词要多写一个字母。

entries.definition: The same noun written with a doubled consonant, normal in the United States and Canada.
entries.definitionCN: 同一个名词的双写形式，在美国与加拿大通用。

entries.definition: Somebody who has been registered; the ending marks the person affected.
entries.definitionCN: 已登记的人；词尾标记动作承受者。

entries.definition: The equivalent noun for joining the armed forces, built on list rather than roll.
entries.definitionCN: 参军的对应名词，造自「清单」而非「名册卷」。

entries.definition: The broad word for entering anything in a register, from cars to conference attendees.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指把任何事物记入登记簿，从汽车到会议听众。

entries.definition: Focuses on being accepted rather than on the paperwork that follows.
entries.definitionCN: 强调被录取，而非随后的手续。

entries.definition: Formal enrolment at a university, still used as a ceremonial term.
entries.definitionCN: 大学的正式注册，现仍作仪式用语。

entries.definition: A reporting phrase for the counted number of participants.
entries.definitionCN: 报道参加人数的统计短语。

normalIntro.en: Enrolment is enrol plus the noun ending, so it names the paperwork of joining.
normalIntro.cn: enrolment 是 enrol 加名词词尾，因此指参加时办的手续。

normal.en: One l in British enrolment, two in American enrollment.
normal.cn: 英式 enrolment 单写，美式 enrollment 双写。

normal.en: The verb keeps the doubling only when the stress falls on the last syllable.
normal.cn: 只有重音落在末音节时动词才双写辅音。

normal.en: Pair it with school, course, scheme: the three typical nouns before it.
normal.cn: 常与 school、course、scheme 搭配，这是最常见的三个前置名词。

normal.en: Enrolment can mean either the act or the headcount, so check the number in the sentence.
normal.cn: 它既可指行为也可指人数，需看句中数字判断。

normal.en: In charts, a fall in enrolment means fewer students, not fewer forms.
normal.cn: 图表中 enrolment 下降指学生变少，而非表格变少。

abstract.en: Picture a ledger opened at the counter, pen in hand.
abstract.cn: 想象柜台前摊开的账簿，手里握着笔。

abstract.en: Imagine a bar chart whose first column is the tallest.
abstract.cn: 想象一张柱状图，第一列最高。

abstract.en: Think of a wristband collected at a health clinic entrance.
abstract.cn: 想想在诊所门口领取的住院手环。

examples.en: Enrolment for the language course is now open.
examples.cn: 语言课程的注册现已开放。

examples.en: A fall in primary school enrolment worried the council.
examples.cn: 小学入学人数下降令市政委员会担忧。

examples.en: Her enrolment in the scheme was confirmed by email.
examples.cn: 她参加该计划已通过邮件确认。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因若满」——名单因登记而填满，所以 enrolment 是注册；这只是拆词联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 rotulus（纸卷）→ 古法语 rolle（名册）＋ en-（使上）→ enroller → 中古英语 enrolen → 现代英语 enrol＋名词词尾 -ment → enrolment，核心义「记入名册」。

sensesIntro.en: The noun covers the act of signing in, the headcount it produces, and the standing membership that results.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个名词涵盖登记行为、行为产生的人数，以及由此形成的在册状态。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a name written into an official roll that is then counted and kept.
core.cn: 核心意象：姓名写进正式名册，随后被清点保存。

branches.en: The paperwork itself is the most concrete sense.
branches.cn: 手续本身，是最具体的义项。

branches.en: The counted total turns the list into statistics.
branches.cn: 清点后的总数把名单变成统计数据。

branches.en: The continuing status applies the idea to benefit schemes.
branches.cn: 持续在籍状态把概念用于福利计划。

branches.en: Both involve an institution holding your name.
branches.cn: 两者都涉及机构保存你的姓名。

branches.en: Headcount and status appear together in policy reports.
branches.cn: 人数与在籍状态常一起出现在政策报告中。

intro.en: The word layers a French prefix, a Germanic noun, and an English nominal ending.
intro.cn: 这个词叠加了法语前缀、日耳曼名词与英语名词词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin rotula is a small wheel, and rotulus is the roll of paper that a list was written on.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 rotula 指小轮，rotulus 指用来书写名单的纸卷。

items.exampleCN: en- 位于 enrol 开头。

items.meaning: the act or number of registering

definition_zh: 使成为奴隶；束缚；使沉迷
definition_en: to make someone a slave, or to keep someone under a force that controls their life
core_image: 铁链扣住手腕，把人从自由的人变成他人手中的财产
scene: 史料记载，沿海村落整批居民被船队运走贩卖。Ship captains enslaved coastal communities for profit.
sceneCN: 这里 enslave 是「使成为奴隶」（第 1 个义项：夺走自由并视为财产）；句意：船长们为牟利而奴役沿岸居民。

senses.title: To make a person the property of another
senses.definition: to take away someone's freedom and treat that person as owned property
senses.definitionCN: 夺走某人的自由并将其视为财产
senses.example: Colonial powers enslaved millions of people.
senses.exampleCN: 殖民势力奴役了数以百万计的人。
senses.why: The prefix en- puts someone into a state, and the state named here is the one slave denotes.
senses.whyCN: 前缀 en- 表示把人置于某种状态，这里就是 slave 所指的状态。

senses.title: To keep someone under a controlling force
senses.definition: to prevent someone from choosing freely because a powerful influence holds them
senses.definitionCN: 因强大力量掌控某人，使其无法自主选择
senses.example: Debt enslaved the small factory owner.
senses.exampleCN: 债务束缚了这家小厂的主人。
senses.why: Figuratively the chain need not be iron: any force that removes real choice can enslave.
senses.whyCN: 引申而言锁链未必是铁的：任何剥夺真实选择权的力量都能构成奴役。

senses.title: To give yourself so completely that a thing rules you
senses.definition: to devote so much time and will to something that it controls your life
senses.definitionCN: 把时间与意志过多交给某事物，以至于被它统治
senses.example: Ambition enslaved the novelist in his final years.
senses.exampleCN: 野心在小说家晚年把他牢牢困住。
senses.why: Applied to feelings and goals, the verb warns that a thing you love can become a master.
senses.whyCN: 用于情感与目标时，这个动词警示：你所爱之物也可能变成主人。

intro.en: Slave reached English through French and German from the name of a people, and en- later built a verb on it.
intro.cn: slave 经法语与德语进入英语，源自一个民族的族名；后来英语用 en- 由它造出动词。

items.en: Slověnin meant a Slav, many of whom were captured in early medieval wars.
items.cn: Slověnin 指斯拉夫人，早期中世纪战争中许多人被俘。

items.en: Sclave came to mean a person bought as a servant.
items.cn: Sclave 转指被买来服役的人。

items.en: Esclave carries the word into French and then into England.
items.cn: esclave 把该词带入法语，随后传入英国。

items.en: Sawle appears in English records of the trade.
items.cn: 中古英语出现 sawle，用于贸易记录。

items.en: Enslave is attested with the literal sense of owning persons.
items.cn: 近古英语中 enslave 有使人沦为奴隶的确证。

items.en: The figurative sense of being ruled by debt or habit becomes common.
items.cn: 现代英语中，被债务或习惯支配的比喻义变得常用。

note.en: Group one holds words built on the same noun; group two holds other verbs of taking freedom.
note.cn: 第一组是同一名词派生的词；第二组是其他剥夺自由的动词。

entries.definition: The noun that supplies the meaning; the prefix only turns it into an action.
entries.definitionCN: 提供核心义的名词；前缀只把它变成动作。

entries.definition: The condition or the historical process named as a fact rather than an act.
entries.definitionCN: 作为事实或过程来表述的状态。

entries.definition: The person who performs the act, preferred in modern historical writing.
entries.definitionCN: 施动者，现代史学写作更倾向使用。

entries.definition: Sounds close but means to settle comfortably, with no link to bondage.
entries.definitionCN: 读音相近，实指安顿舒适，与奴役无关。

entries.definition: To catch in a snare; the loss is of freedom of movement rather than of personhood.
entries.definitionCN: 陷入罗网，失去的是行动自由而非人格。

entries.definition: Historically to hold in thrall; now often means to captivate delightfully.
entries.definitionCN: 史指处于束缚，今常指令人着迷。

entries.definition: To bring a people under rule, closer to political control than to ownership.
entries.definitionCN: 使一个民族臣服，更近政治统治而非所有权。

entries.definition: The condition itself rather than the act of imposing it.
entries.definitionCN: 指处境本身，而非施加该处境的行为。

normalIntro.en: Enslave is en plus slave, so the verb literally means to put someone into slavery.
normalIntro.cn: enslave 是 en 加 slave，因此字面义是把人置于奴役状态。

normal.en: Read it as make a slave of, and the grammar follows at once.
normal.cn: 读作「使成为奴隶」，语法随即清楚。

normal.en: Passive voice is common: enslaved by debt, enslaved by habit.
normal.cn: 被动式常见：被债务奴役、被习惯奴役。

normal.en: Historical writing now prefers enslaver over slave owner for the buyer side.
normal.cn: 史学写作现更倾向用 enslaver 取代 slave owner。

normal.en: The figurative use keeps the violence of the literal one, so it is strong words.
normal.cn: 比喻用法保留本义的暴力色彩，因此语气很重。

normal.en: Pair with a people, a workforce, or a self, the three usual objects.
normal.cn: 常见宾语是民族、劳工群体或自身。

abstract.en: Picture an iron ring closing around an ankle.
abstract.cn: 想象铁环在脚踝上扣紧。

abstract.en: Imagine a ledger of bills that decides every meal a family eats.
abstract.cn: 想象一叠账单决定一家人每餐吃什么。

abstract.en: Think of a desk lamp burning at dawn while the writer has not slept.
abstract.cn: 想想天未亮书桌灯仍亮着，而作者一夜未眠。

examples.en: Millions were enslaved and transported across the ocean.
examples.cn: 数以百万计的人被奴役并运过大洋。

examples.en: He felt enslaved by his own obligations.
examples.cn: 他觉得自己被责任束缚住了。

examples.en: Addiction can enslave even the wealthy.
examples.cn: 成瘾甚至能让富人也沦为俘虏。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因死累屋」——因为死累而困在屋里出不去，所以 enslave 是奴役；这只是拆词联想，与词源无关。

root: 斯拉夫语 Slověnin（斯拉夫人）→ 中古高地德语 Sclave → 古法语 esclave → 中古英语 slave＋前缀 en-（使进入）→ 现代英语 enslave，核心义「使人沦为奴隶」。

sensesIntro.en: The verb moves from owning persons, to being controlled by forces such as debt, to being ruled by one's own passions.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个动词从占有他人，到被债务之类力量控制，再到被自身欲望支配。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a chain fastened to someone who did not choose it.
core.cn: 核心意象：锁链扣在一个并未同意的人身上。

branches.en: Physical ownership is the historical base sense.
branches.cn: 人身占有是对应的历史义项。

branches.en: Economic pressure supplies a modern figurative chain.
branches.cn: 经济压力提供了现代的比喻锁链。

branches.en: Inner compulsion turns the self into both captive and captor.
branches.cn: 内在强迫使自我同时成为囚徒与看守。

branches.en: Both senses remove the possibility of refusal.
branches.cn: 两个义项都剥夺拒绝的可能。

branches.en: Debt and passion alike can dictate a whole life.
branches.cn: 债务与欲望都能支配人的一生。

intro.en: A productive English prefix is attached to a borrowed noun, and the family grows with English endings.
intro.cn: 英语能产前缀加在借入名词上，词族由英语词尾扩展。

latinIntro.en: Medieval Latin sclavus and dux are the written forms behind the word for a Slav and for a leader.
latinIntro.cn: 中古拉丁语 sclavus 与 dux 分别是斯拉夫人与首领的书面形式。

items.exampleCN: en- 由 slave 造出 enslave。

items.meaning: a Slav, later a bonded person
items.meaningCN: 斯拉夫人，后指被束缚者
items.example: Sclavus is the written Latin form.
items.exampleCN: sclavus 是对应的拉丁书写形式。

items.example: Dis- gives the rare verb disenslave.
items.exampleCN: dis- 构成罕见动词 disenslave。
serf 指相关的一种处境。

items.example: Vassal sits between free and enslaved.
items.exampleCN: vassal 介于自由与奴役之间。

definition_zh: 随后发生；作为结果而产生
definition_en: to happen after something else, often as a direct result of it
core_image: 多米诺骨牌倒下第一张，后面那一张跟着倒下
scene: 庄稼歉收之后，饥荒随之而来。Starvation ensued when the harvest failed.
sceneCN: 这里 ensue 是「随之发生」（第 1 个义项：在时间上接续发生）；句意：庄稼歉收后饥荒随之而来。

derivatives.zh: 结果；随之而来（古旧用法）

senses.title: To happen afterwards in time
senses.definition: to take place after some earlier event, without necessarily naming a cause
senses.definitionCN: 在先前的事件之后发生，未必点明原因
senses.example: A long silence ensued after the announcement.
senses.exampleCN: 宣布之后陷入长久的沉默。
senses.why: The old meaning of the root is to follow, so the verb places one event behind another on a timeline.
senses.whyCN: 词根本义为跟随，因此该动词把两个事件排在时间线的前后。

senses.title: To follow as a result
senses.definition: to happen because of something that has just occurred
senses.definitionCN: 由于刚发生的事件而产生
senses.example: Injury ensued from the careless manoeuvre.
senses.exampleCN: 这次莽撞动作导致了受伤。
senses.why: When sequence is read as cause, the word shifts from what comes next to what comes because of the earlier thing.
senses.whyCN: 当先后关系被读作因果时，词义从「接下来」转向「因此」。

intro.en: Ensue follows a Latin verb meaning to come after, carried into English by French.
intro.cn: ensue 来自表示「紧随其后」的拉丁动词，经法语进入英语。

items.en: Sequi means to follow, the root inside consequent and sequence.
items.cn: sequi 意为跟随，是 consequent 与 sequence 的词根。

items.en: Insequi was reshaped into a form with the stress on the second syllable.
items.cn: insequi 被改造为重音落在第二音节的形式。

items.en: Ensuir means to follow or to result.
items.cn: ensuir 意为跟随或产生结果。

items.en: Ensuen enters religious and legal translation.
items.cn: 中古英语 ensuen 出现在宗教与法律译文。

items.en: The verb stays formal and prefers the participle ensuing.
items.cn: 该动词保持正式语体，更常用分词 ensuing。

note.en: Group one holds relatives of the same Latin root; group two holds other verbs of resulting.
note.cn: 第一组是同一拉丁词根的同族词；第二组是其他表示结果的动词。

entries.definition: One letter apart but entirely different: this verb means to make certain.
entries.definitionCN: 只差一个字母却意义迥异：该动词表确保。

entries.definition: The usual adjective form, as in the ensuing weeks.
entries.definitionCN: 常用的分词形容词，如随后数周。

entries.definition: The noun from the same following root, but it names the result itself.
entries.definitionCN: 同根名词，指结果本身。

entries.definition: A story that follows another, keeping the idea of coming after.
entries.definitionCN: 接续前作的故事，保留「在后」之义。

entries.definition: The plain verb for coming after; ensue is its formal equivalent.
entries.definitionCN: 表在后的日常动词，ensue 是其正式对应。

entries.definition: To appear or develop, often from a cause named by from.
entries.definitionCN: 出现或产生，常与 from 搭配。

entries.definition: To happen because of something, usually with from or in.
entries.definitionCN: 因某事而发生，多接 from 或 in。

entries.definition: To develop out of an earlier source, with the image of a plant stem.
entries.definitionCN: 由更早源头长出，取植物茎干意象。

normalIntro.en: Ensue looks like ensure but has no sure inside: read it as follow instead.
normalIntro.cn: ensue 形似 ensure，内部却没有 sure：应读作「跟随其后」。

normal.en: Nothing can ensue a thing; the event itself is the subject.
normal.cn: ensue 不带宾语，主语就是发生的事件。

normal.en: Say ensued from when a cause is named.
normal.cn: 点明原因时说 ensued from。

normal.en: The participle ensuing is far more common than the finite verb.
normal.cn: 分词 ensuing 比限定动词常用得多。

normal.en: Use it for unwelcome chains: chaos, injury, argument.
normal.cn: 多用于不快的连锁：混乱、受伤、争吵。

normal.en: Avoid the passive; nothing is ensued by someone.
normal.cn: 不要用被动，没有人被 ensue。

abstract.en: Picture dominoes tipping one after another across a table.
abstract.cn: 想象骨牌在桌面上依次倾倒。

abstract.en: Imagine smoke arriving after the spark.
abstract.cn: 想象火星之后升起的烟。

abstract.en: Think of an echo that only comes once the shout has ended.
abstract.cn: 想想只在喊声结束后才出现的回声。

examples.en: A fierce debate ensued over the new fee.
examples.cn: 围绕新费用爆发了激烈辩论。

examples.en: Complications ensued, and the operation was delayed.
examples.cn: 随后出现并发症，手术被迫推迟。

examples.en: Little good ensued from the hasty decision.
examples.cn: 这个仓促决定几乎没带来好处。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因思悠」——因为结果令人思绪悠长，所以 ensue 是随之而来；这只是拆词联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 sequi（跟随）→ 俗拉丁语 insequi → 古法语 ensuir → 中古英语 ensuen → 现代英语 ensue，核心义「跟在后面发生」。

sensesIntro.en: Both senses come after something: one marks time alone, the other adds a causal relation.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项都在他事之后：一个只表时间先后，另一个加上因果关系。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the second card falling because the first one did.
core.cn: 核心意象：第一张牌倒下，第二张随之倒下。

branches.en: Pure time sequence is the older, neutral sense.
branches.cn: 单纯的时间先后是更早、更中性的义项。

branches.en: Causal reading supplies the modern formal use.
branches.cn: 因果解读构成现代正式用法。

branches.en: Both place the new event behind an old one.
branches.cn: 两者都把新事件排在旧事件之后。

branches.en: With from, the verb behaves like result from.
branches.cn: 搭配 from 时该动词近似 result from。

branches.en: The participle ensuing turns sequence into a time label.
branches.cn: 分词 ensuing 把先后关系变成时间标签。

intro.en: The verb is a prefix plus a Latin root of following, and its family spreads through French and English endings.
intro.cn: 该动词由前缀加表示跟随的拉丁词根构成，词族经法语与英语词尾扩展。

latinIntro.en: Latin sequi means to follow, and its participles give English words such as sequela and subsequent.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 sequi 意为跟随，其分词派生出 sequela 与 subsequent 等词。

items.exampleCN: en- 位于 ensue 开头。

items.example: The noun survived only in old texts.
items.exampleCN: 该名词只存留于旧文献。
con- 与前缀不同而词根相同。

definition_zh: 确保；保证；使必然发生
definition_en: to make certain that something happens or is true
core_image: 用手把门闩牢牢扣上，让事情没有出岔子的余地
scene: 出发前她把清单又核对了一遍，确认每件行李都上了车。She checked the list again to ensure that every bag was on the bus.
sceneCN: 这里 ensure 是「确保」（第 1 个义项：使某事必然发生）；句意：她又核对了一遍清单，以确保每件行李都上了车。

senses.title: To make certain an outcome
senses.definition: to take action so that something certainly happens
senses.definitionCN: 采取行动，使某事确定发生
senses.example: Please ensure that the door is locked before you leave.
senses.exampleCN: 离开前请确保门已锁好。
senses.why: The word is built on sure, so the verb literally means to make an outcome sure.
senses.whyCN: 这个词建立在 sure 之上，因此动词字面上就是「使结果确定」。

senses.title: To protect or guarantee
senses.definition: to make a person or right safe from harm or unfair treatment
senses.definitionCN: 使某人或某项权利免受伤害或不公平对待
senses.example: The new rules ensure fair treatment for all workers.
senses.exampleCN: 新规定保障所有工人得到公平对待。
senses.why: Protecting people is the same certainty applied to their safety and rights.
senses.whyCN: 保护人，就是把同样的「确定」用于他们的安全与权利。

senses.title: To secure a result in advance
senses.definition: to arrange conditions so that a desired result can be secured
senses.definitionCN: 事先安排好条件，使期望的结果有把握到来
senses.example: Hard work does not ensure success, but it improves the chances.
senses.exampleCN: 努力不能确保成功，但能提高成功的可能。
senses.why: Here the word points to securing the way things turn out, not to a legal promise.
senses.whyCN: 这里指把事情的走向「锁定」，而不是法律意义上的承诺。

intro.en: Ensure comes from Anglo-Norman enseurer, from Old French asseürer, to assure, built on Latin securus, free from care.
intro.cn: ensure 来自盎格鲁-诺曼语 enseurer，源于古法语 asseürer（使确信），建立在拉丁语 securus（无忧的）之上。

items.en: Securus means free from care, from se-, apart, and cura, care.
items.cn: securus 意为无忧的，由 se-（脱离）与 cura（忧虑）构成。

items.en: Assecurare means to make safe or free from worry.
items.cn: assecurare 意为使安全、使无忧。

items.en: Asseürer carries the meaning to assure or make certain.
items.cn: asseürer 意为使确信、使有保证。

items.en: Enseurer develops the en- form used in English law and trade.
items.cn: enseurer 发展出英语法律与商业中使用的 en- 形式。

items.en: Middle English ensuren means to make safe or certain.
items.cn: 中古英语 ensuren 意为使安全或使确定。

items.en: Modern English uses ensure mainly for making an outcome certain.
items.cn: 现代英语中，ensure 主要用于表示「使结果确定」。

note.en: Ensure belongs to the sure family, and it sits near verbs for guaranteeing and securing.
note.cn: ensure 属于「确定」词族，与表示保证和确保的动词相邻。

entries.definition: to protect against loss with an insurance policy
entries.definitionCN: 给……保险

entries.definition: to tell someone confidently that something is true
entries.definitionCN: 向……保证

entries.definition: a confident promise or belief
entries.definitionCN: 保证；信心

entries.definition: to promise that something will certainly happen
entries.definitionCN: 保证；担保

entries.definition: to make something safe or certain
entries.definitionCN: 使安全；确保

entries.definition: to make a fact or arrangement certain
entries.definitionCN: 确认；证实

normalIntro.en: Ensure contains sure: the whole point of the verb is to make an outcome sure.
normalIntro.cn: ensure 含有 sure：这个动词的全部要点就是让结果「确定」。

normal.en: En- turns the adjective sure into a verb meaning make sure.
normal.cn: 前缀 en- 把形容词 sure 变成动词，意为「使确定」。

normal.en: Ensure that is the most common pattern, and it is followed by a full clause.
normal.cn: ensure that 是最常见的搭配，后面接完整从句。

normal.en: Keep ensure and insure apart: one makes certain, the other buys insurance.
normal.cn: 把 ensure 与 insure 分开：一个表示使确定，另一个表示买保险。

normal.en: Compare assure: assure works on people, while ensure works on outcomes.
normal.cn: 对比 assure：assure 的对象是人，ensure 的对象是结果。

normal.en: In formal writing, ensure often replaces make sure.
normal.cn: 在正式写作中，ensure 常用来替代 make sure。

abstract.en: Picture a latch clicked shut, so the door cannot swing open in the night.
abstract.cn: 想象门闩咔嗒扣上，夜里门再也吹不开。

abstract.en: Imagine checking every seat belt before the bus leaves.
abstract.cn: 想象大巴出发前逐条检查安全带。

abstract.en: Think of a knot pulled tight so the load cannot slip.
abstract.cn: 想象绳结被拉紧，货物不会滑脱。

examples.en: The nurse ensured that the patient was comfortable.
examples.cn: 护士确保病人躺得舒服。

examples.en: Regular checks ensure the machines run safely.
examples.cn: 定期检查确保机器安全运转。

examples.en: To ensure a seat, book your ticket early.
examples.cn: 想确保有座位，就早点订票。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因 sure」——因为确定，所以 ensure 就是确保；这只是拆词联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 securus（无忧的）→ 俗拉丁语 assecurare（使安全）→ 古法语 asseürer → 盎格鲁-诺曼语 enseurer → 中古英语 ensuren → 现代英语 ensure，核心义「使确定无疑」。

sensesIntro.en: The word moves from freedom from care to the act of making an outcome certain, then to legal and practical guarantees.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词从「无忧」出发，转到「使结果确定」的动作，再延伸到法律与实际层面的保障。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a latch fastened so that the outcome cannot slip away.
core.cn: 核心意象：门闩扣紧，结果无法溜走。

branches.en: Making an outcome certain is the everyday core sense.
branches.cn: 使结果确定，是日常的核心义项。

branches.en: Protecting people or rights extends the same certainty into safety.
branches.cn: 保护人或权利，把同样的确定延伸到安全。

branches.en: Securing a result means arranging the conditions in advance.
branches.cn: 确保得到结果，就是事先安排条件。

branches.en: Certainty and safety are two sides of the same promise.
branches.cn: 确定与安全是同一个承诺的两面。

branches.en: Protection and advance planning often appear together in rules.
branches.cn: 保护与事前规划常一起出现在规则里。

intro.en: Ensure is a French-shaped verb with a Latin core, and its small family grows with English endings.
intro.cn: ensure 是法语形态的动词，核心来自拉丁语，其小词族由英语词尾扩展。

latinIntro.en: Latin cura means care, securus means free from care, and assecurare means to make safe.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 cura 表示忧虑，securus 表示无忧，assecurare 表示使安全。

items.exampleCN: en- 出现在 ensure 与 enlarge 开头。

items.example: Securus is the deep root behind ensure.
items.exampleCN: securus 是 ensure 背后的深层词根。

items.example: Se- in securus means apart from care.
items.exampleCN: securus 中的 se- 意为脱离忧虑。

items.example: Cura supplies the idea of care.
items.exampleCN: cura 提供「关心、忧虑」的意思。
assecurare 把两部分连接起来。

items.example: Asseürer carries the verb into French.
items.exampleCN: asseürer 把这个动词带入法语。

items.example: Enseurer gives English its en- form.
items.exampleCN: enseurer 为英语提供 en- 形式。

items.meaningCN: 表示动作或状态的名词词尾

items.example: Ensurance is now archaic or rare.
items.exampleCN: ensurance 现在已古旧或罕见。

definition_zh: 牵涉；需要；使成为必要结果；限定继承
definition_en: to involve something as a necessary part or result, or to require effort, cost, or time
core_image: 一份清单上，主任务后面用线串着几项不可避免的子任务
scene: 调往新岗位意味着要长期驻外，还要重新学习一套系统。The assignment entails long stays abroad.
sceneCN: 这里 entail 是「牵涉；需要」（第 1 个义项：作为必要部分伴随而来）；句意：这项任务牵涉长期驻外。

pos.zh: 牵涉；需要；使成为必然结果
限定继承；被限定的遗产

derivatives.zh: 限定遗产的授予者（法律用语）

senses.title: To involve something as a necessary part
senses.titleCN: 牵涉；包含作为必要部分
senses.definition: to have something as an unavoidable part of a plan, role, or situation
senses.definitionCN: 把某事物作为计划、职位或情境中不可避免的一部分
senses.example: The job entails a great deal of travelling.
senses.exampleCN: 这份工作需要大量出差。
senses.why: The old legal verb cut an estate so that duties came attached to it, so part of the sense is always something tied on.
senses.whyCN: 该词的法律古义是把产业连同义务一起划定，因此词义始终带有附带绑定的意味。

senses.title: To require effort, cost, or time
senses.definition: to make something necessary because of what follows from it
senses.definitionCN: 因其后果而使某事物成为必需
senses.example: Repairs will entail replacing the whole floor.
senses.exampleCN: 维修意味着更换整块地板。
senses.why: When the attached part is a price or labour, the verb shifts from containing to demanding.
senses.whyCN: 当附带的部分是代价或劳动时，动词从包含转向要求。

senses.title: To limit inheritance to fixed heirs
senses.definition: to settle property so that it can pass only to specified descendants
senses.definitionCN: 安排财产仅由指定后裔继承
senses.example: The estate was entailed to the eldest son.
senses.exampleCN: 这份遗产被限定由长子继承。
senses.why: This is the original legal use: the notch cut on a tally stick fixed who could inherit next.
senses.whyCN: 这是最初的法律用法：在计数木条上刻出的缺口规定了下一位继承人。

intro.en: Entail began as a law term about cutting a tail of heirs onto an estate, from French tailler.
intro.cn: entail 原是法律术语，指为产业切出继承人的尾部，来自法语 tailler。

items.en: Taxiare gave the idea of cutting or arranging by notches.
items.cn: taxiare 给出刻痕整理之义。

items.en: Tailler means to cut, and taille is a notch or tally.
items.cn: tailler 意为切割，taille 指刻痕或计数条。

items.en: Entailler describes fixing the tail of heirs of a property.
items.cn: entailler 指固定财产的继承人序列。

items.en: The verb enters English charters and land records.
items.cn: 中古英语中该动词进入特许状与土地文书。

items.en: Figurative uses attach unavoidable conditions to plans.
items.cn: 近古英语时期出现把必然条件附于计划的比喻用法。

items.en: The general sense of involving as a necessity now dominates.
items.cn: 现代英语以「作为必要而牵涉」的通义为主。

note.en: Group one holds the noun and the rhyming borrowings; group two holds other verbs of necessity.
note.cn: 第一组是名词与同尾借词；第二组是其他表示必要的动词。

entries.definition: The noun, used for a legal settlement and for a relation between propositions.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，指限定继承与命题间的蕴含关系。

entries.definition: Same ending sound, different history: selling goods in small quantities.
entries.definitionCN: 尾部同音而来源不同，指零售。

entries.definition: Built on the same French verb for cutting off a share, here a small part described closely.
entries.definitionCN: 同样源自表切割的法语动词，指细述的小部分。

entries.definition: The stick with notches that lies behind the legal image.
entries.definitionCN: 背后刻缺口的木条，正是法律意象的来源。

entries.definition: The everyday verb for including as part; entail stresses necessity more.
entries.definitionCN: 表包含的日常动词，entail 更强调必然性。

entries.definition: To need by rule or nature, without the image of attached consequences.
entries.definitionCN: 按规则或本性需要，不含附带后果的意象。

entries.definition: To make necessary, a formal rival used in reports.
entries.definitionCN: 使成为必需，是报告语体中的正式竞争词。

entries.definition: To take something as a condition before it happens.
entries.definitionCN: 把某事物事先当作条件。

normalIntro.en: Entail can be read as en plus tail: a duty follows at the tail of every action.
normalIntro.cn: entail 可读作 en 加 tail：每项行动的尾巴上都跟着义务。

normal.en: Subject is a task or situation; object is the attached cost or labour.
normal.cn: 主语多为任务或情境，宾语为附带的代价或劳动。

normal.en: Entail takes a noun or an -ing form, never an infinitive.
normal.cn: entail 接名词或动名词，不接不定式。

normal.en: In law the noun entailment and the verb both keep the inheritance sense.
normal.cn: 法律上名词 entailment 与动词都保留继承义。

normal.en: Reports prefer entails to involves when the point is unavoidable cost.
normal.cn: 强调不可避免的代价时，报告体更用 entails。

normal.en: Remember the tail image: what hangs behind the action.
normal.cn: 记住尾巴意象：挂在行动之后的东西。

abstract.en: Picture a wagon hooked behind a horse that did not ask for it.
abstract.cn: 想象马身后被挂上一辆它并未要求的货车。

abstract.en: Imagine a tally stick whose notches bind the next heir.
abstract.cn: 想象刻着缺口、束缚下一位继承人的计数木条。

abstract.en: Think of a price tag sewn inside the collar of a new plan.
abstract.cn: 想想新方案领口内缝着的价签。

examples.en: The redesign entails rewriting every test.
examples.cn: 重新设计意味着重写所有测试。

examples.en: Such a merger would entail heavy legal costs.
examples.cn: 这样的合并将带来高昂的法律费用。

examples.en: Teaching young children entails patience above all.
examples.cn: 教幼儿最需要的品质是耐心。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因台尔」——因为台上一句话，台下要跑腿，所以 entail 是牵涉、需要；这只是拆词联想，与词源无关。

root: 高卢罗马语 *taxiare → 古法语 tailler（切）＋ en- → 盎格鲁-诺曼法语 entailler（为产业切定继承人）→ 中古英语 entaillen → 现代英语 entail，核心义「附带而不可分」。

sensesIntro.en: The verb grew out of a legal device for binding inheritance and now names anything that unavoidably comes attached.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个动词源于绑定继承的法律手段，如今指任何必然附随而来的事物。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a tail that cannot be cut off from the body of the plan.
core.cn: 核心意象：无法从计划主体上割下的尾巴。

branches.en: Any plan carries parts that cannot be avoided.
branches.cn: 任何计划都带有无法回避的部分。

branches.en: When the attached part is cost, the verb means demand.
branches.cn: 附随之物是代价时，动词转为要求。

branches.en: The legal sense binds heirs to an estate.
branches.cn: 法律义把继承人与产业绑定。

branches.en: Both describe a link that cannot be broken.
branches.cn: 两者都描述无法切断的关联。

branches.en: Obligation appears in budgets and in inheritance alike.
branches.cn: 义务既出现在预算中，也出现在继承中。

intro.en: A French prefix joins a French verb stem, and the family extends with English nominal endings.
intro.cn: 法语前缀接法语动词词干，词族由英语名词词尾延伸。

latinIntro.en: Late Latin taxare means to assess or arrange by notches, the learned ancestor of the French stem.
latinIntro.cn: 晚期拉丁语 taxare 指以刻痕估价或整理，是法语词干的书面前身。

items.exampleCN: en- 位于 entail 开头。

items.example: Taille names the mark cut in wood.
items.exampleCN: taille 指在木上刻出的记号。

items.example: The phrase records the original use.
items.exampleCN: 该短语记录了最初用法。

items.meaning: a binding condition or logical relation
items.example: Entailment is used in logic texts.

items.meaning: a small part cut off and described
items.exampleCN: detail 与 entail 共享法语词干。

definition_zh: 肠炎；肠道炎症
definition_en: inflammation of the lining of the intestine, often causing pain and diarrhoea
core_image: 肠壁内侧发红肿胀，像被热水烫过的管道内壁
scene: 幼犬连续两天腹泻，兽医在化验后确诊为肠炎。The puppy was treated for enteritis after two days of diarrhoea.
sceneCN: 这里 enteritis 是「肠炎」（第 1 个义项：肠道黏膜的炎症）；句意：这只幼犬在接受肠炎治疗。

senses.title: Inflammation of the intestine
senses.definition: a medical condition in which the wall of the intestine becomes inflamed and painful
senses.definitionCN: 肠壁发炎并伴疼痛的疾病状态
senses.example: Enteritis can follow a bacterial infection.
senses.exampleCN: 细菌感染之后可能引发肠炎。
senses.why: The name is built from the Greek word for intestine plus the inflammation ending used across medicine.
senses.whyCN: 这个词由表示肠的希腊语加上医学通用的炎症词尾构成。

senses.title: A named disease in young animals or infants
senses.definition: a specific inflammatory disease, often necrotising, that affects neonates and livestock
senses.definitionCN: 多发于新生幼崽与家畜的特定炎症性疾病，常伴组织坏死
senses.example: Necrotising enteritis is a risk in premature babies.
senses.exampleCN: 坏死性肠炎是早产儿面临的风险之一。
senses.why: Veterinary and neonatal usage narrows the general name to one recognised syndrome.
senses.whyCN: 兽医与新生儿医学把泛称收窄为一种公认病症。

senses.title: A combining element in compound disease names
senses.titleCN: 构词成分；复合病名后缀
senses.definition: the element -itis attached to entero- inside compounds such as gastroenteritis
senses.definitionCN: entero- 与炎症词尾 -itis 在胃肠炎等复合词中的构词成分
senses.example: Gastroenteritis combines the stomach and gut names.
senses.exampleCN: gastroenteritis 把胃与肠的名称合为一体。
senses.why: Because the parts are productive, the same shape reappears wherever a gut inflammation must be named.
senses.whyCN: 由于这两个成分都能产新词，凡需命名肠道炎症时同一形态都会再现。

intro.en: The word joins a Greek noun for intestine with a Greek ending that medicine uses for inflammation.
intro.cn: 这个词把表示肠的希腊名词与医学表炎症的希腊词尾拼在一起。

items.en: Enteron means gut or intestine.
items.cn: enteron 指肠道。

items.en: The ending itis marked a pathological condition.
items.cn: 词尾 -itis 标记病变状态。

items.en: Medical Latin wrote enteritis as a fixed diagnostic term.
items.cn: 近代拉丁医学文书把 enteritis 写成固定诊断术语。

items.en: English clinical texts adopt the word alongside gastritis.
items.cn: 十九世纪英语临床文本采纳该词，与 gastritis 并用。

items.en: Veterinary usage extends it to named syndromes in animals.
items.cn: 现代英语中兽医用法把它延伸到动物特定病症。

note.en: Group one holds the same-ending inflammation names; group two holds close clinical terms.
note.cn: 第一组是同一炎症词尾的病名；第二组是相近的临床说法。

entries.definition: The same ending applied to the stomach rather than the intestine.
entries.definitionCN: 同一词尾用于胃而非肠。

entries.definition: Inflammation limited to the colon, a narrower site than the general gut term.
entries.definitionCN: 炎症限于结肠，部位比泛称更窄。

entries.definition: Named for the lower small intestine specifically.
entries.definitionCN: 专指小肠下段的炎症。

entries.definition: Relating to the intestines, as in an enteric coating.
entries.definitionCN: 肠的，如肠溶包衣。

entries.definition: The body's response itself, without locating the organ.
entries.definitionCN: 机体的炎症反应本身，不定位器官。

entries.definition: Invasion by germs, which may lead to the inflammation but is not the same thing.
entries.definitionCN: 病原体侵入，可引发炎症但并非同一概念。

entries.definition: The combined condition, common in everyday travel advice.
entries.definitionCN: 胃肠同时发炎，常见于旅行健康提示。

entries.definition: A long-term clinical category rather than a single acute episode.
entries.definitionCN: 长期临床类别，而非一次急性发作。

normalIntro.en: Split the word into entero, gut, and itis, the medical ending for inflammation.
normalIntro.cn: 把词拆成 entero（肠）与 itis（医学炎症词尾）。

normal.en: Every -itis word names one inflamed place: joint, stomach, gut.
normal.cn: 所有 -itis 词都指某一部位发炎：关节、胃、肠。

normal.en: Enteritis is usually uncountable, so no plural is needed.
normal.cn: enteritis 通常不可数，无需复数。

normal.en: Travel writing prefers gastroenteritis, which adds the stomach.
normal.cn: 旅行类文章更常用 gastroenteritis，其中加入了胃。

normal.en: Veterinary reports say necrotising enteritis for the severe form.
normal.cn: 兽医报告用 necrotising enteritis 表示重症。

normal.en: Do not confuse enteric the adjective with enteritis the disease.
normal.cn: 不要混淆形容词 enteric 与病名 enteritis。

abstract.en: Picture a pipe whose inner wall has turned red and swollen.
abstract.cn: 想象一段管道，内壁已经发红肿胀。

abstract.en: Imagine a diagram of the gut lit up in warning colour.
abstract.cn: 想象一张肠道示意图被警示色点亮。

abstract.en: Think of a fever chart whose label ends in the same four letters.
abstract.cn: 想想体温记录单上以同样四个字母结尾的标签。

examples.en: The child was hospitalised with severe enteritis.
examples.cn: 这个孩子因重症肠炎住院。

examples.en: Bacterial enteritis spreads through contaminated water.
examples.cn: 细菌性肠炎经污染水源传播。

examples.en: Rest and fluids are the standard care for enteritis.
examples.cn: 休息与补液是肠炎的常规护理。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「安肠赖提死」——肠道不安宁拖累人，所以 enteritis 是肠炎；这只是拆词联想，与词源无关。

root: 希腊语 ἕντερον / enteron（肠）＋ -itis（炎症）→ 近代拉丁医学语 enteritis → 现代英语 enteritis，核心义「肠道发炎」。

sensesIntro.en: The term names an inflamed gut, narrows to specific syndromes, and works as a productive element in compound disease names.
sensesIntro.cn: 该词既指肠道发炎，也可收窄为特定病症，还能作为构词成分进入复合病名。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the inner lining of the intestine reddened and swollen.
core.cn: 核心意象：肠内壁发红肿胀。

branches.en: The clinical name for an inflamed intestine.
branches.cn: 肠炎的临床名称。

branches.en: Specialised fields attach a named syndrome to it.
branches.cn: 专门领域为它附上具体病症名。

branches.en: The parts keep building new compound names.
branches.cn: 两个成分继续构造新的复合病名。

branches.en: Both share the idea of inflamed gut tissue.
branches.cn: 两者都以肠壁组织发炎为核心。

branches.en: Severe forms and compounds appear together in veterinary texts.
branches.cn: 重症与复合词在兽医文献中并见。

intro.en: This is a wholly classical build: a Greek combining form plus a Greek medical ending.
intro.cn: 这是完全古典语构成的词：希腊组合形式加希腊医学词尾。

latinIntro.en: Medical Latin wrote enteron and -itis unchanged, which is how the parts reached English textbooks.
latinIntro.cn: 医学拉丁语原样书写 enteron 与 -itis，这两个成分由此进入英语教材。

items.exampleCN: entero- 位于 enteropathy 开头。

items.example: Enteron is the base of the name.
Enteric coating dissolves in the gut.

items.exampleCN: 该形容词修饰重症类型。

definition_zh: 企业；事业；进取心
definition_en: a business or bold project, or the initiative needed to undertake one
core_image: 一队人带着工具走出城门，去把一桩有风险的大事做成
scene: 小镇上那家做太阳能板的企业去年雇了三十名工人。The enterprise that makes solar panels in the town hired thirty workers last year.
sceneCN: 这里 enterprise 是「企业」（第 1 个义项：从事经营活动的组织）；句意：镇上那家生产太阳能板的企业去年雇了三十名工人。

derivatives.zh: 有进取心的；有事业心的

senses.title: A business organization
senses.definition: a company or business, especially a commercial one
senses.definitionCN: 公司或商业组织，尤指营利性的
senses.example: The family runs a small printing enterprise.
senses.exampleCN: 这家人经营着一家小型印刷企业。
senses.why: An enterprise is first something undertaken, and a business is the most common thing undertaken in modern life.
senses.whyCN: enterprise 本指「所承担之事」，而现代生活中最常见的承担之事就是经营。

senses.title: A bold or difficult project
senses.definition: an ambitious project that involves effort and risk
senses.definitionCN: 需要付出努力并承担风险的宏大计划
senses.example: Building the bridge was a bold enterprise.
senses.exampleCN: 修建这座桥是一项大胆的事业。
senses.why: The original French noun names something undertaken, so any large risky task fits.
senses.whyCN: 法语原名词指「着手去做的事」，因此任何宏大而冒险的任务都符合。

senses.title: Initiative and boldness
senses.definition: the quality of being willing to start new and difficult things
senses.definitionCN: 愿意开创全新而困难之事的品质
senses.example: She showed great enterprise in opening the shop.
senses.exampleCN: 她开这家店，表现出很强的进取心。
senses.why: The willingness to undertake is abstracted into a personal quality.
senses.whyCN: 「敢于承担」被抽象为一种个人品质。

intro.en: Enterprise comes from Old French entreprise, something undertaken, from entreprendre, to take in hand, built on Latin inter and prehendere.
intro.cn: enterprise 来自古法语 entreprise（所承担之事），源于 entreprendre（着手去做），由拉丁语 inter 与 prehendere 构成。

items.en: Inter means between or among.
items.cn: inter 意为在……之间。

items.en: Prehendere means to seize or take hold of.
items.cn: prehendere 意为抓住、握住。

items.en: Entreprendre means to undertake or take in hand.
items.cn: entreprendre 意为着手、承担。

items.en: Entreprise names the thing undertaken.
items.cn: entreprise 指所承担的事情。

items.en: Middle English enterprise covers bold deeds as well as business.
items.cn: 中古英语 enterprise 既指大胆行动，也指商业经营。

items.en: Modern English separates the business, project, and initiative senses.
items.cn: 现代英语分化出企业、事业与进取心三个义项。

note.en: Enterprise is an undertaking noun, and it sits near its own derivatives and near words for business and ventures.
note.cn: enterprise 是一个「承担之事」名词，与自身派生词以及表示商业和冒险事业的词相邻。

entries.definition: willing to start new and bold things
entries.definitionCN: 有进取心的

entries.definition: a person who starts a business
entries.definitionCN: 企业家；创业者

entries.definition: the activity of starting businesses
entries.definitionCN: 创业活动；企业家精神

entries.definition: a company or commercial activity
entries.definitionCN: 企业；生意

entries.definition: an organization that sells goods or services
entries.definitionCN: 公司

entries.definition: a new project involving risk
entries.definitionCN: 冒险事业；创业项目

normalIntro.en: Enterprise contains prise, from French prendre, to take: it is the taking up of a task.
normalIntro.cn: enterprise 含有 prise，来自法语 prendre（拿取）：它就是「把事情接过来做」。

normal.en: Entre- means between, and prendre means take: taking something in hand.
normal.cn: entre- 表示之间，prendre 表示拿取：把事情接到手里。

normal.en: A business enterprise is an undertaking that must pay its way.
normal.cn: 商业企业是一项必须自己养活自己的事业。

normal.en: Spirit of enterprise names the courage to start something risky.
normal.cn: spirit of enterprise 指敢于开创冒险之事的勇气。

normal.en: Entrepreneur is the person, while enterprise is the thing or the quality.
normal.cn: entrepreneur 是人，enterprise 是事情或品质。

normal.en: Compare venture: both involve risk, but enterprise also means a company.
normal.cn: 对比 venture：两者都含风险，但 enterprise 还可指公司。

abstract.en: Picture a group setting out at dawn with tools and a map.
abstract.cn: 想象一队人带着工具和地图，在黎明出发。

abstract.en: Imagine a merchant signing a contract on a busy quay.
abstract.cn: 想象一位商人在繁忙的码头上签下合同。

abstract.en: Think of a seed pushed into hard ground before any shoot appears.
abstract.cn: 想象一粒种子被按进硬土，嫩芽尚未出现。

examples.en: The family runs a small printing enterprise.
examples.cn: 这家人经营着一家小型印刷企业。

examples.en: Building the bridge was a bold enterprise.
examples.cn: 修建这座桥是一项大胆的事业。

examples.en: She showed great enterprise in opening the shop.
examples.cn: 她开这家店，表现出很强的进取心。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「enter prize」——敢进场去拿奖，就是有进取心的事业；这只是拆词联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 inter（之间）＋ prehendere（抓取）→ 古法语 entreprendre（着手做）→ entreprise（所承担之事）→ 中古英语 enterprise → 现代英语 enterprise。

sensesIntro.en: The noun begins as something taken in hand, then narrows to a business, widens to any bold project, and finally names the courage behind it.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个名词最初指「接到手里的事」，随后收窄为商业企业，又扩展为任何大胆事业，最后指背后的勇气。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a group setting out to take a risky task in hand.
core.cn: 核心意象：一队人出发，把有风险的任务接到手里。

branches.en: A business is the most concrete modern undertaking.
branches.cn: 企业是现代社会最具体的「承担之事」。

branches.en: A bold project keeps the original sense of something undertaken.
branches.cn: 大胆事业保留「所承担之事」的原义。

branches.en: Initiative is the personal quality that starts undertakings.
branches.cn: 进取心是开创事业所需的个人品质。

branches.en: A company and a large project both require planning and risk.
branches.cn: 公司与大型项目都需要规划与冒险。

branches.en: Bold projects exist because someone supplies the initiative.
branches.cn: 大胆事业之所以存在，是因为有人提供进取心。

intro.en: Enterprise is a French noun built from entre and prendre, with English endings forming its modern family.
intro.cn: enterprise 是由 entre 与 prendre 构成的法语名词，现代词族由英语词尾扩展。

latinIntro.en: Latin inter means between, and prehendere means to seize; French entreprendre joins them.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 inter 表示之间，prehendere 表示抓取；法语 entreprendre 把两者结合。

items.exampleCN: entre- 出现在 entreprendre 与 enterprise 开头。

items.example: Inter is the Latin source of entre-.
items.exampleCN: inter 是 entre- 的拉丁语来源。

items.example: Prehendere is the deep root of prendre.
items.exampleCN: prehendere 是 prendre 的深层词根。

items.example: Entreprendre means to take something in hand.
items.exampleCN: entreprendre 意为把事情接到手里。

items.example: Entreprise is the direct source of enterprise.
items.exampleCN: entreprise 是 enterprise 的直接来源。
enterprise 保留「承担之事」的含义。

items.example: Enterprising describes a person or plan.
Entrepreneur names the person who undertakes.

items.meaningCN: 表示状态或品质的词尾

definition_zh: 使娱乐；招待；怀有（想法）
definition_en: to amuse people, to receive guests, or to keep an idea in mind
core_image: 主人张开双臂把客人迎进屋，让他们坐下、吃喝、笑出声
scene: 晚饭后爷爷讲了一个长笑话，把孩子们逗得直笑。Grandpa told a long joke after dinner and entertained the children for an hour.
sceneCN: 这里 entertain 是「使娱乐」（第 1 个义项：让人开心消遣）；句意：晚饭后爷爷讲了一个长笑话，逗得孩子们笑了一个小时。

senses.title: To amuse and hold attention
senses.definition: to give people pleasure and keep them interested
senses.definitionCN: 给人快乐并让他们保持兴趣
senses.example: The clown entertained the crowd for an hour.
senses.exampleCN: 小丑逗了观众一个小时。
senses.why: The old sense of holding someone is applied to holding their attention pleasantly.
senses.whyCN: 古老的「留住某人」之意，被用来表示愉快地留住他们的注意力。

senses.title: To receive guests
senses.definition: to welcome guests and provide food, drink, or company
senses.definitionCN: 迎接客人并提供饮食或陪伴
senses.example: They entertained friends at home all weekend.
senses.exampleCN: 整个周末他们都在家招待朋友。
senses.why: Hospitality is the oldest social sense: keeping people together in your house.
senses.whyCN: 待客是最古老的社交义项：把人们留在自己家里相聚。

senses.title: To hold an idea in mind
senses.definition: to consider or keep an idea, hope, or doubt in your mind
senses.definitionCN: 在心里考虑或保留某种想法、希望或疑虑
senses.example: He refused to entertain the idea of moving abroad.
senses.exampleCN: 他拒绝考虑移居国外的想法。
senses.why: The mind is pictured as a host that can receive and hold a thought.
senses.whyCN: 心智被想象成一位可以接纳并留住想法的主人。

intro.en: Entertain comes from Old French entretenir, to hold together or maintain, from entre, between, and tenir, to hold.
intro.cn: entertain 来自古法语 entretenir（使相聚、维持），由 entre（之间）与 tenir（握住）构成。

items.en: Tenere means to hold or keep.
items.cn: tenere 意为握住、保持。

items.en: Tenir continues the Latin verb for holding.
items.cn: tenir 延续拉丁语中表示「握住」的动词。

items.en: Entretenir means to hold together and keep up.
items.cn: entretenir 意为使相聚、维持。

items.en: Middle English entretinen means to keep up or maintain.
items.cn: 中古英语 entretinen 意为维持、保持。

items.en: The sense of amusing guests and audiences becomes common.
items.cn: 到 17 世纪，招待客人、娱乐观众的意思流行起来。

items.en: Modern English keeps the amusement, hospitality, and mental senses together.
items.cn: 现代英语把娱乐、招待与心中怀有三个义项并存。

note.en: Entertain is a holding verb, and it sits near its own family and near words for amusing and hosting.
note.cn: entertain 是一个「留住」动词，与自身词族以及表示逗乐和待客的词相邻。

entries.definition: shows or activities that amuse people
entries.definitionCN: 娱乐；娱乐活动

entries.definition: a person who amuses an audience
entries.definitionCN: 表演者

entries.definition: amusing and enjoyable
entries.definitionCN: 有趣的

entries.definition: to make someone laugh or smile
entries.definitionCN: 逗乐

entries.definition: to receive and look after guests
entries.definitionCN: 招待；主办

entries.definition: to keep a thought or feeling in mind
entries.definitionCN: 怀有（想法或情感）

normalIntro.en: Entertain goes back to French tenir, to hold: it holds a guest's attention and keeps it.
normalIntro.cn: entertain 可追溯到法语 tenir（握住）：它把客人的注意力握住并留住。

normal.en: Enter- means between, and tenir means hold: to hold someone in a pleasant state.
normal.cn: enter- 表示之间，tenir 表示握住：把某人留在愉快的状态里。

normal.en: Entertain guests is the older hospitality sense.
normal.cn: entertain guests 是更古老的待客义项。

normal.en: Entertain an idea is to hold it in the mind for a while.
normal.cn: entertain an idea 是把想法在心里留一会儿。

normal.en: Entertainment is the noun, and entertainer is the person.
normal.cn: entertainment 是名词，entertainer 是人。

normal.en: Compare amuse: amuse makes people laugh, while entertain can also mean to host.
normal.cn: 对比 amuse：amuse 让人发笑，而 entertain 还可表示招待。

abstract.en: Picture a host holding open the door while plates are passed around.
abstract.cn: 想象主人扶着门，盘子在客人之间传递。

abstract.en: Imagine a juggler keeping five balls in the air.
abstract.cn: 想象杂耍者让五个球停在空中。

abstract.en: Think of a thought held lightly in the palm before it is accepted.
abstract.cn: 想象一个想法被轻轻托在掌心，尚未被接受。

examples.en: The clown entertained the crowd for an hour.
examples.cn: 小丑逗了观众一个小时。

examples.en: They entertained friends at home all weekend.
examples.cn: 整个周末他们都在家招待朋友。

examples.en: He refused to entertain the idea of moving abroad.
examples.cn: 他拒绝考虑移居国外的想法。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「enter + ten」——把客人请进门，再用十成的热情留住他，就是招待与娱乐；这只是拆词联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 tenere（握住）→ 古法语 entretenir（维持、使相聚）→ 中古英语 entretinen → 现代英语 entertain，由「留住、维持」引申为招待与娱乐。

sensesIntro.en: The verb first means to keep something together, then to keep guests, then to keep attention amused, and finally to keep an idea in mind.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个动词先表示「维持在一起」，再表示留住客人，继而表示留住注意力使人开心，最后表示把想法留在心里。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: guests held in a warm circle of food, talk, and laughter.
core.cn: 核心意象：客人被留在饮食、交谈与笑声组成的温暖圈子里。

branches.en: Amusing people is holding their attention pleasantly.
branches.cn: 逗人开心，就是愉快地留住注意力。

branches.en: Hospitality keeps guests physically and socially close.
branches.cn: 待客让客人在身体与社交上保持亲近。

branches.en: Holding an idea keeps it in the mind as a guest.
branches.cn: 怀有想法，就是把它当作客人留在心里。

branches.en: A good host both feeds guests and keeps them amused.
branches.cn: 好主人既招待饮食，也让客人开心。

branches.en: Receiving people and receiving ideas both use the same holding image.
branches.cn: 接纳人与接纳想法使用同一个「留住」意象。

intro.en: Entertain is a French verb rebuilt on a Latin root, and English endings carry it into noun and adjective forms.
intro.cn: entertain 是建立在拉丁词根上的法语动词，英语词尾把它扩展到名词与形容词。

latinIntro.en: Latin tenere means to hold, and French entretenir means to hold together or keep up.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 tenere 表示握住，法语 entretenir 表示使相聚、维持。
