definition_zh: 娱乐；娱乐活动；招待
definition_en: shows, activities, or hospitality that amuse people or look after guests
core_image: 灯光、音乐与笑声组成的一整晚，还有摆满食物的餐桌
scene: 演出开始前，剧场经理说今晚的娱乐节目会持续到午夜。Before the show began, the theatre manager said the evening's entertainment would last until midnight.
sceneCN: 这里 entertainment 是「娱乐节目」（第 1 个义项：使人开心的演出或活动）；句意：演出开始前，剧场经理说今晚的娱乐节目会持续到午夜。

senses.title: Shows and activities that amuse
senses.definition: films, music, games, or other things that give people pleasure
senses.definitionCN: 电影、音乐、游戏等给人快乐的事物
senses.example: The hotel offers live entertainment every evening.
senses.exampleCN: 这家酒店每晚都有现场娱乐表演。
senses.why: The noun names the things produced when people are entertained.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词指人们被娱乐时所产生的事物。

senses.title: The act of entertaining guests
senses.definition: the activity of welcoming and looking after guests
senses.definitionCN: 迎接并照顾客人的活动
senses.example: Their hospitality was more than mere entertainment.
senses.exampleCN: 他们的好客不只是表面的招待。
senses.why: The old hospitality sense of the verb survives in the noun.
senses.whyCN: 动词古老的待客义项在名词中保留下来。

senses.title: A performance or event
senses.definition: a particular show or event that people watch for pleasure
senses.definitionCN: 人们为消遣而观看的某场演出或活动
senses.example: The concert was good entertainment for the whole family.
senses.exampleCN: 这场音乐会对全家来说都是很好的消遣。
senses.why: One instance of amusing activity is counted as a piece of entertainment.
senses.whyCN: 一次具体的娱乐活动，就算作一件娱乐节目。

intro.en: Entertainment is entertain plus the noun ending -ment; the verb comes from Old French entretenir, to hold together.
intro.cn: entertainment 是 entertain 加名词词尾 -ment；动词来自古法语 entretenir（使相聚、维持）。

items.en: Tenere means to hold or keep.
items.cn: tenere 意为握住、保持。

items.en: Entretenir means to hold together and maintain.
items.cn: entretenir 意为使相聚、维持。

items.en: Middle English entretinen gives the base verb.
items.cn: 中古英语 entretinen 提供基础动词。

items.en: The noun entertainment appears for hospitality and amusement.
items.cn: 到 16 世纪，名词 entertainment 出现，表示招待与娱乐。

items.en: Public shows and the entertainment industry expand the word.
items.cn: 到 19 世纪，公共演出与娱乐业扩展了这个词的用法。

items.en: Modern English uses entertainment for both shows and hospitality.
items.cn: 现代英语中，entertainment 既指节目，也指待客。

note.en: Entertainment is the -ment noun of entertain, and it sits near its family and near words for amusement and shows.
note.cn: entertainment 是 entertain 的 -ment 名词，与自身词族以及表示娱乐和演出的词相邻。

entries.definition: to amuse or receive guests
entries.definitionCN: 娱乐；招待

entries.definition: a person who amuses an audience
entries.definitionCN: 表演者

entries.definition: amusing and enjoyable
entries.definitionCN: 有趣的

entries.definition: the feeling of finding something funny or enjoyable
entries.definitionCN: 愉悦；消遣

entries.definition: a performance for an audience
entries.definitionCN: 演出

entries.definition: activity done for pleasure when not working
entries.definitionCN: 消遣；娱乐

normalIntro.en: Entertainment is entertain plus -ment, so it names the pleasure and the shows that result from entertaining.
normalIntro.cn: entertainment 是 entertain 加 -ment，指招待与娱乐所带来的快乐和节目。

normal.en: The ending -ment turns the verb into the activity or its result.
normal.cn: 词尾 -ment 把动词变成活动或活动的结果。

normal.en: The entertainment industry is built on holding attention.
normal.cn: 娱乐业建立在「留住注意力」之上。

normal.en: Live entertainment means performers in front of a real audience.
normal.cn: live entertainment 指真人在观众面前表演。

normal.en: For entertainment is the phrase that names the purpose.
normal.cn: for entertainment 是说明目的的常用短语。

normal.en: Compare amusement: amusement is often the feeling, while entertainment is often the show.
normal.cn: 对比 amusement：amusement 常指感受，entertainment 常指节目。

abstract.en: Picture a theatre before the curtain rises, seats filling with chatter.
abstract.cn: 想象大幕拉开前的剧场，座位间满是交谈声。

abstract.en: Imagine a table cleared for cards and laughter after dinner.
abstract.cn: 想象晚饭后桌子被清出来打牌，笑声不断。

abstract.en: Think of a band tuning up while the lights dim.
abstract.cn: 想象灯光变暗，乐队正在调音。

examples.en: The hotel offers live entertainment every evening.
examples.cn: 这家酒店每晚都有现场娱乐表演。

examples.en: Their hospitality was more than mere entertainment.
examples.cn: 他们的好客不只是表面的招待。

examples.en: The concert was good entertainment for the whole family.
examples.cn: 这场音乐会对全家来说都是很好的消遣。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「entertain + ment」——把人留住、让人开心的那件事，就是娱乐；这只是构词联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 tenere（握住）→ 古法语 entretenir（使相聚、维持）→ 中古英语 entretinen → entertain（招待、娱乐）＋ -ment → entertainment（娱乐；招待）。

sensesIntro.en: The noun covers the feeling and activity of being amused, the old duty of looking after guests, and the concrete shows that produce pleasure.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个名词涵盖被娱乐的感受与活动、古老的待客职责，以及产生快乐的具体节目。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an evening of lights, music, and laughter shared with others.
core.cn: 核心意象：灯光、音乐与笑声共享的一晚。

branches.en: Shows and games are the most visible form of entertainment.
branches.cn: 演出与游戏是最显眼的娱乐形式。

branches.en: Hospitality is entertainment in its oldest social form.
branches.cn: 待客是娱乐最古老的社交形式。

branches.en: A single performance is counted as one entertainment.
branches.cn: 一场演出可算作一项娱乐活动。

branches.en: The industry produces events, and each event is an entertainment.
branches.cn: 娱乐业生产活动，每场活动就是一项娱乐。

branches.en: A host's evening and a public show both aim at pleasure.
branches.cn: 主人的晚宴与公开演出都以快乐为目标。

intro.en: Entertainment is an English -ment noun built on the French-shaped verb entertain.
intro.cn: entertainment 是建立在法语形态动词 entertain 上的英语 -ment 名词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin core is tenere, to hold; French entretenir keeps people together, and English adds -ment.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁核心是 tenere（握住）；法语 entretenir 使人相聚，英语再加 -ment。

items.exampleCN: entre- 出现在 entretenir 开头。

items.meaningCN: 表示动作或结果的词尾

items.example: Entertainment names the activity and its result.

definition_zh: 热情；热忱；热衷的事物
definition_en: a strong feeling of excitement and interest in something
core_image: 胸口像被一团火点着，忍不住向前倾身去做那件事
scene: 听说球队要打决赛，整条街的人都兴奋地讨论起来。When the team reached the final, the whole street discussed it with enthusiasm.
sceneCN: 这里 enthusiasm 是「热情」（第 1 个义项：强烈的兴奋与兴趣）；句意：球队打进决赛时，整条街的人都热情地讨论这件事。

senses.title: Strong excitement and interest
senses.definition: a strong feeling of eagerness and interest in something
senses.definitionCN: 对某事物强烈的渴望与兴趣
senses.example: She spoke about the project with great enthusiasm.
senses.exampleCN: 她满腔热情地谈起这个项目。
senses.why: The Greek source describes a god within, and that inner fire becomes strong excited interest.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语来源描述「心中有神」，这种内心之火就变成强烈的兴奋与兴趣。

senses.title: An object of passionate interest
senses.definition: an activity or subject that someone pursues with great eagerness
senses.definitionCN: 某人满怀热忱去从事的活动或主题
senses.example: Gardening is one of her lifelong enthusiasms.
senses.exampleCN: 园艺是她终身的爱好之一。
senses.why: The feeling is transferred to the thing that produces it.
senses.whyCN: 这种情感被转移到产生它的事物上。

senses.title: Fervent devotion to a cause
senses.definition: intense and sometimes uncritical devotion to a belief or cause
senses.definitionCN: 对信念或事业强烈、有时缺乏批判的投入
senses.example: His early enthusiasm for the movement later cooled.
senses.exampleCN: 他早年对这场运动的狂热后来冷却了。
senses.why: The original religious intensity survives in this formal sense of devoted zeal.
senses.whyCN: 原初的宗教强度保留在这个正式的「热诚」义项中。

intro.en: Enthusiasm comes from Greek enthousiasmos, divine possession, from entheos, having a god within, built on en- and theos, god.
intro.cn: enthusiasm 来自希腊语 enthousiasmos（神灵附体），源于 entheos（心中有神），由 en- 与 theos（神）构成。

items.en: Theos means god.
items.cn: theos 意为神。

items.en: Entheos means having a god within, inspired.
items.cn: entheos 意为心中有神、受神灵启发的。

items.en: Enthousiasmos means divine possession or inspired frenzy.
items.cn: enthousiasmos 意为神灵附体、受神启的狂热。

items.en: Enthusiasmus carries the term into learned Latin.
items.cn: enthusiasmus 把这个词带入学术拉丁语。

items.en: English adopts enthusiasm for possession by a god.
items.cn: 到 16 世纪，英语用 enthusiasm 表示神灵附体。

items.en: The word now means strong excited interest in almost anything.
items.cn: 现代英语中，这个词表示对几乎任何事物的强烈兴趣。

note.en: Enthusiasm is a fire word, and it sits near its own family and near words for passion and zeal.
note.cn: enthusiasm 是一个「火焰」词，与自身词族以及表示激情和热忱的词相邻。

entries.definition: a person who is very interested in something
entries.definitionCN: 热衷者；爱好者

entries.definition: showing strong excitement
entries.definitionCN: 热情的

entries.definition: in an eager and excited way
entries.definitionCN: 热情地

entries.definition: a very strong feeling or interest
entries.definitionCN: 激情；热爱

entries.definition: great energy for a cause
entries.definitionCN: 热忱；干劲

entries.definition: the state of wanting something very much
entries.definitionCN: 渴望；急切

normalIntro.en: Enthusiasm comes from Greek entheos, having a god within: the word pictures fire inside a person.
normalIntro.cn: enthusiasm 来自希腊语 entheos（心中有神）：这个词描绘人体内的一团火。

normal.en: Theos means god, so enthusiasm once meant divine possession.
normal.cn: theos 意为神，所以 enthusiasm 原指神灵附体。

normal.en: Modern enthusiasm is simply strong excitement and interest.
normal.cn: 现代的 enthusiasm 就是强烈的兴奋与兴趣。

normal.en: Enthusiasm for something is the usual pattern with a noun.
normal.cn: enthusiasm for something 是常见的名词搭配。

normal.en: The adjective is enthusiastic, and the person is an enthusiast.
normal.cn: 形容词是 enthusiastic，指人是 enthusiast。

normal.en: Compare passion: passion burns quietly, while enthusiasm shows itself openly.
normal.cn: 对比 passion：passion 安静地燃烧，enthusiasm 则外露。

abstract.en: Picture a spark catching dry grass and spreading fast.
abstract.cn: 想象火星落在干草上，迅速蔓延。

abstract.en: Imagine a child pulling a parent toward a festival tent.
abstract.cn: 想象孩子拉着父母往节日的帐篷跑。

abstract.en: Think of a room leaning forward to hear one voice.
abstract.cn: 想象整个房间的人都前倾身体听一个声音。

examples.en: She spoke about the project with great enthusiasm.
examples.cn: 她满腔热情地谈起这个项目。

examples.en: His enthusiasm for music began at school.
examples.cn: 他对音乐的热情始于学校。

examples.en: The crowd's enthusiasm lifted the players.
examples.cn: 观众的热情鼓舞了球员。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「en-theos」——心里住着一位神，所以热情高涨；这只是词源拆解式联想，与日常读音无关。

root: 希腊语 theos（神）→ entheos（心中有神的）→ enthousiasmos（神灵附体般的激情）→ 拉丁语 enthusiasmus → 英语 enthusiasm。

sensesIntro.en: The word begins as divine possession, softens into religious fervor, and finally becomes the everyday fire of strong interest.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词最初指神灵附体，后淡化为宗教热诚，最终成为日常所说的强烈兴趣之火。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a fire lit inside a person that pushes them forward.
core.cn: 核心意象：心中燃起一团火，推着人向前。

branches.en: Strong excited interest is the everyday modern sense.
branches.cn: 强烈兴奋的兴趣，是现代日常义项。

branches.en: The thing that lights the fire becomes an enthusiasm too.
branches.cn: 点燃火焰的事物本身也被称作 enthusiasm。

branches.en: Devotion to a cause keeps the original intensity.
branches.cn: 对事业的投入保留了原初的强度。

branches.en: People feel enthusiasm, and their hobbies are their enthusiasms.
branches.cn: 人怀有热情，而爱好就是他们所热衷的事物。

branches.en: A lifelong hobby and a cause can both command devotion.
branches.cn: 终身爱好与事业都能赢得投入。

intro.en: Enthusiasm is a Greek word that reached English through Latin, and English endings form its modern family.
intro.cn: enthusiasm 是经拉丁语进入英语的希腊词，现代词族由英语词尾构成。

latinIntro.en: Greek theos means god, and entheos means having a god within; Latin enthusiasmus carries the word westward.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语 theos 表示神，entheos 表示心中有神；拉丁语 enthusiasmus 把这个词带向西方。

items.exampleCN: en- 出现在 entheos 开头。

items.example: Theos is the heart of the word.
Entheos gives the image of inner fire.
items.exampleCN: entheos 提供内心之火的画面。

items.example: Enthousiasmos is the direct Greek source.
items.exampleCN: enthousiasmos 是直接的希腊语来源。

items.example: Enthusiasmus carries the term into Latin.
items.exampleCN: enthusiasmus 把这个词带入拉丁语。

items.example: Enthusiasm is the modern English form.

items.meaningCN: 表示状态或做法的词尾
items.example: The noun keeps the Greek -ismos shape.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词保留希腊语 -ismos 的形态。

items.example: Enthusiastic adds -ic to the noun stem.

definition_zh: 热衷者；狂热爱好者；笃信者
definition_en: a person who is extremely interested in and active about a subject or activity
core_image: 展览馆里一个人围着同一件展品转了三圈，逢人便讲它的来历
scene: 每到观星季，他都在山顶守着望远镜到天亮。He is an enthusiast of amateur astronomy.
sceneCN: 这里 enthusiast 是「狂热爱好者」（第 1 个义项：对某活动极有兴趣并投入其中的人）；句意：他是业余天文爱好者。

senses.title: A person devoted to an activity
senses.definition: someone who spends time and energy on a hobby or subject because they love it
senses.definitionCN: 因喜爱而在某项爱好或主题上投入时间与精力的人
senses.example: Local enthusiasts restored the old railway.
senses.exampleCN: 当地爱好者修复了这条老铁路。
senses.why: The word first named a person filled with divine inspiration, so the modern hobbyist keeps that sense of being possessed by an interest.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最早指被神灵灵感充满的人，因此今天的爱好者仍保留被兴趣占据的意味。

senses.title: An active supporter of a cause
senses.definition: a person who works eagerly for a political or social idea
senses.definitionCN: 热切投身某种政治或社会理念的人
senses.example: The campaign relied on committed enthusiasts.
senses.exampleCN: 这场运动依靠坚定的积极分子。
senses.why: Moved from hobby to cause, the noun stresses belief and effort rather than pleasure.
senses.whyCN: 从爱好转向事业后，这个名词强调信念与投入，而非乐趣。

senses.title: A person claimed to be inspired from above
senses.titleCN: 灵恩狂信者（历史宗教义）
senses.definition: in older religious writing, someone who professed direct inspiration by a deity
senses.definitionCN: 在早期宗教文献中指声称受神灵直接启示的人
senses.example: Critics dismissed the preacher as an enthusiast.
senses.exampleCN: 批评者称这位布道者为狂信者。
senses.why: This is the oldest sense: god within, a person moved by a power they cannot control.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的义项：神明在内，人被自身无法控制的力量推动。

intro.en: Enthusiast literally means having a god within, from Greek en and theos.
intro.cn: enthusiast 字面义是内有神明，来自希腊语 en 与 theos。

items.en: En theos means with a god or inspired.
items.cn: en theos 意为有神附身、受启示。

items.en: Enthousiasmos named the state of being possessed.
items.cn: enthousiasmos 指被神灵附体的状态。

items.en: Entusiasmus carries the term into learned Latin.
items.cn: entusiasmus 是该词的拉丁写法。

items.en: Enthousiaste gives the English its modern shape.
items.cn: enthousiaste 为英语提供现代词形。

items.en: English uses it as a criticism of religious excess.
items.cn: 十七世纪英语用以批评宗教狂热。

items.en: The word softens into the neutral hobbyist sense.
items.cn: 现代英语中该词淡化，成为中性的爱好者义。

note.en: Group one holds the family built on the same stem; group two holds other words for keen people.
note.cn: 第一组是同一词干的同族词；第二组是其他指热心者的词。

entries.definition: The emotion itself, while the person noun names someone moved by it.
entries.definitionCN: 指情感本身，而指人的词表示被这种情感驱动者。

entries.definition: The adjective of the same family, far more common in daily speech.
entries.definitionCN: 同族形容词，日常口语远比名词常用。

entries.definition: Built on the same Greek word for god, but it names a belief rather than a temper.
entries.definitionCN: 同样基于表神的希腊语，但指信仰而非性情。

entries.definition: A doctrinal label sharing the same person suffix.
entries.definitionCN: 共享同一人物词尾的教义标签。

entries.definition: Someone devoted to a person or cause, with loyalty rather than energy stressed.
entries.definitionCN: 忠于某人或某事者，强调忠诚而非热情。

entries.definition: An enthusiastic amateur with real knowledge, as in a history buff.
entries.definitionCN: 懂行的热心业余者，如历史迷。

entries.definition: A Spanish borrowing for a devoted fan of a defined field.
entries.definitionCN: 借自西班牙语，指某领域的忠实爱好者。

entries.definition: Much stronger and mostly negative: someone uncompromising in a cause.
entries.definitionCN: 语气强得多且多为贬义，指狂热党派者。

normalIntro.en: Split enthusiast into en plus theia, a god, so the person originally had a god inside.
normalIntro.cn: 把 enthusiast 拆成 en 与 theia（神），因此这人原本内有神明。

normal.en: The person is an enthusiast; the feeling is enthusiasm.
normal.cn: 人叫 enthusiast，情感叫 enthusiasm。

normal.en: Say enthusiast for something, rarely for somebody.
normal.cn: 常说某事的 enthusiast，很少说某人的。

normal.en: In reviews it is a compliment; in older religious texts it was an accusation.
normal.cn: 在评论中它是褒义，在旧宗教文献中却是指责。

normal.en: The adjective enthusiastic is neutral and safe in essays.
normal.cn: 形容词 enthusiastic 中性，写作可放心使用。

normal.en: Countable noun: two enthusiasts, not two enthusiasm.
normal.cn: 可数名词：two enthusiasts，不是 two enthusiasm。

abstract.en: Picture a visitor who cannot leave a single exhibit.
abstract.cn: 想象一位在一件展品前舍不得离开的观众。

abstract.en: Imagine a lantern carried through the town long after the festival ends.
abstract.cn: 想象节日结束后仍在城中提着灯笼的人。

abstract.en: Think of a trembling figure said to speak with a voice not its own.
abstract.cn: 想想古人所说颤抖着、以非自身声音说话的人。

examples.en: He became an enthusiast for urban cycling.
examples.cn: 他成了城市骑行的热心者。

examples.en: Car enthusiasts meet at the depot each Sunday.
examples.cn: 车迷每个周日在车库集合。

examples.en: She is a keen enthusiast of silent films.
examples.cn: 她是默片的忠实爱好者。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因谁求济事」——因为谁来都急着帮忙做事，所以 enthusiast 是热心者；这只是拆词联想，与词源无关。

root: 希腊语 en（在内）＋ theos（神）→ enthousios（有神附身）→ enthousiasmos → 拉丁语 enthusiasmus → 法语 enthousiaste → 英语 enthusiast，核心义「内心被点燃的人」。

sensesIntro.en: The noun runs from religious possession to eager support of a cause and finally to the ordinary hobbyist.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个名词从宗教性的神灵附体，走向对事业的热切支持，最后落到日常的爱好者。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a fire lit inside a person that shows in everything they do.
core.cn: 核心意象：人内心燃起的火，显现在他做的一切之中。

branches.en: Ordinary devotion to a hobby is the modern core.
branches.cn: 对爱好的投入是现代核心用法。

branches.en: Causes borrow the same energy in a public form.
branches.cn: 事业以公共形式借用同一种能量。

branches.en: The oldest sense still appears in histories of religion.
branches.cn: 最古义项仍见于宗教史著作。

branches.en: Both describe someone ruled by an inner impulse.
branches.cn: 两者都描述被内在冲动支配的人。

branches.en: Conviction links the campaigner to the inspired preacher.
branches.cn: 信念把运动者与受启示的布道者相连。

intro.en: A Greek compound of with plus god is extended by English person and quality endings.
intro.cn: 希腊语「神在内」的复合词由英语人物与性质词尾扩展。

latinIntro.en: Latin Deus and Greek Theos both name god, and both feed English words such as deism and theology.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 deus 与希腊语 theos 都表神，分别进入 deism 与 theology 等英语词。

items.exampleCN: en- 位于希腊复合词开头。

items.example: The adjective is the direct ancestor.

definition_zh: 热情的；热心的
definition_en: showing strong excitement and interest
core_image: 眼睛里发亮，身体前倾，抢着把喜欢的事说给别人听
scene: 新来的志愿者一进门就热情地介绍起周末的活动安排。The new volunteer was enthusiastic about the weekend programme from the moment she arrived.
sceneCN: 这里 enthusiastic 是「热情的」（第 1 个义项：表现出强烈兴趣）；句意：新志愿者一进门就对周末的活动安排充满热情。

senses.title: Showing strong eager interest
senses.definition: showing a lot of excitement and interest in something
senses.definitionCN: 对某事物表现出大量兴奋与兴趣
senses.example: The children were enthusiastic about the trip.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们对这次旅行充满热情。
senses.why: The -ic adjective turns the inner fire of enthusiasm into a visible quality.
senses.whyCN: -ic 形容词把 enthusiasm 的内心之火变成看得见的品质。

senses.title: Eager to take part
senses.definition: very willing to join an activity or help
senses.definitionCN: 非常愿意参加活动或提供帮助
senses.example: The volunteers were enthusiastic about starting work at once.
senses.exampleCN: 志愿者们恨不得马上开始工作。
senses.why: Eagerness to act is enthusiasm directed at doing something.
senses.whyCN: 急于行动，就是指向做事的热情。

senses.title: Expressing warm approval
senses.definition: showing strong and warm support for a plan or idea
senses.definitionCN: 对计划或想法表现出强烈而热烈的支持
senses.example: The plan won enthusiastic support from the whole team.
senses.exampleCN: 这项计划赢得了全队的热烈支持。
senses.why: Approval becomes enthusiastic when it is expressed with the same heat as interest.
senses.whyCN: 当赞同以与兴趣同样的热度表达出来，就成了「热烈赞同」。

intro.en: Enthusiastic is enthusiasm with the adjective ending -ic, from Greek entheos, having a god within.
intro.cn: enthusiastic 是 enthusiasm 加形容词词尾 -ic，源于希腊语 entheos（心中有神）。

items.en: Theos means god, and entheos means inspired by a god.
items.cn: theos 意为神，entheos 意为受神启发的。

items.en: Enthousiasmos means divine possession or inspired fervor.
items.cn: enthousiasmos 意为神灵附体或受神启的热忱。

items.en: Enthusiasmus brings the noun into Latin learning.
items.cn: enthusiasmus 把这个名词带入拉丁学术。

items.en: Enthusiasm enters English with its religious intensity.
items.cn: 到 17 世纪，enthusiasm 带着宗教强度进入英语。

items.en: The ending -ic forms enthusiastic as a describing word.
items.cn: 到 18 世纪，词尾 -ic 构成形容词 enthusiastic。

items.en: Enthusiastic now describes visible eagerness in any field.
items.cn: 现代英语中，enthusiastic 描述任何领域中看得见的热情。

note.en: Enthusiastic is the -ic adjective of enthusiasm, and it sits near its family and near words for eager and keen.
note.cn: enthusiastic 是 enthusiasm 的 -ic 形容词，与自身词族以及表示渴望和热切的词相邻。

entries.definition: strong excited interest
entries.definitionCN: 热情；热忱

entries.definition: a person who is very interested
entries.definitionCN: 热衷者

entries.definition: in an eager way
entries.definitionCN: 热情地

entries.definition: wanting to do something very much
entries.definitionCN: 渴望的

entries.definition: very interested and enthusiastic
entries.definitionCN: 热切的；热衷的

entries.definition: having very strong feelings
entries.definitionCN: 充满激情的

normalIntro.en: Enthusiastic is enthusiasm turned into an adjective with -ic.
normalIntro.cn: enthusiastic 是 enthusiasm 加 -ic 变成的形容词。

normal.en: Drop -ism and add -ic: the noun becomes the describing word.
normal.cn: 去掉 -ism 加上 -ic，名词就变成形容词。

normal.en: Enthusiastic about is the most common pattern.
normal.cn: enthusiastic about 是最常见的搭配。

normal.en: An enthusiastic response is louder than a polite one.
normal.cn: enthusiastic response 比礼貌性的回应更热烈。

normal.en: The adverb enthusiastically adds -ally to the adjective.
normal.cn: 副词 enthusiastically 在形容词后加 -ally。

normal.en: Compare keen: keen is quieter and more common in British English.
normal.cn: 对比 keen：keen 更含蓄，在英式英语中更常见。

abstract.en: Picture hands raised before the question is finished.
abstract.cn: 想象问题还没问完，手已经举起来。

abstract.en: Imagine a door thrown open for a guest.
abstract.cn: 想象门被猛地拉开迎接客人。

abstract.en: Think of a face lit by a screen at midnight.
abstract.cn: 想象午夜时分被屏幕照亮的一张脸。

examples.en: The children were enthusiastic about the trip.
examples.cn: 孩子们对这次旅行充满热情。

examples.en: She gave an enthusiastic welcome to the guests.
examples.cn: 她热情地欢迎客人。

examples.en: His enthusiastic support helped the plan succeed.
examples.cn: 他的热情支持帮助计划取得成功。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「enthusiasm + tic」——热情像小动作一样藏不住，一阵一阵往外冒；这只是拆词联想，与词源无关。

root: 希腊语 theos（神）→ entheos（心中有神的）→ enthousiasmos（受神启的激情）→ 拉丁语 enthusiasmus → 英语 enthusiasm ＋ -ic → enthusiastic。

sensesIntro.en: The adjective describes the outer signs of the inner fire: bright interest, readiness to act, and warm approval.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个形容词描述内心之火的外在迹象：明亮的兴趣、随时行动的意愿，以及热烈的赞同。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a lit face leaning forward, eager to speak or act.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张发亮的脸向前倾，急着说话或行动。

branches.en: Visible interest is the basic adjective sense.
branches.cn: 看得见的兴趣，是形容词的基本义项。

branches.en: Readiness to act turns interest into participation.
branches.cn: 随时行动的意愿把兴趣变成参与。

branches.en: Warm approval directs the same energy at a plan.
branches.cn: 热烈赞同把同样的能量指向一项计划。

branches.en: An interested person usually wants to join in.
branches.cn: 有兴趣的人通常想参与。

branches.en: Eager helpers often give loud support.
branches.cn: 热心的帮手常常给出响亮的支持。

intro.en: Enthusiastic is enthusiasm reshaped with the adjective ending -ic.
intro.cn: enthusiastic 是 enthusiasm 加上形容词词尾 -ic 构成的。

latinIntro.en: Greek theos, god, lies behind the whole family, and the -ic ending is English.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语 theos（神）是整个词族的根源，-ic 词尾则来自英语。

items.exampleCN: en- 出现在 entheos 开头。

items.example: Theos is the heart of the family.
items.exampleCN: theos 是这个词族的核心。

items.example: Entheos supplies the image of inner fire.
items.exampleCN: entheos 提供内心之火的画面。

items.example: Enthousiasmos is the Greek noun source.
items.exampleCN: enthousiasmos 是希腊语名词来源。

items.example: Enthusiastic describes a person or response.

definition_zh: 引诱；诱使；怂恿
definition_en: to persuade someone to do something by offering something attractive
core_image: 猎人把一串亮闪闪的诱饵挂在陷阱入口，引动物自己走近
scene: 商家用低价体验课吸引新用户注册。Low-priced trial lessons entice new customers.
sceneCN: 这里 entice 是「引诱；诱使」（第 1 个义项：以好处吸引人行动）；句意：低价体验课吸引新顾客。

senses.title: To lure by offering something attractive
senses.definition: to draw someone toward an action by showing them a pleasure or advantage
senses.definitionCN: 以展示某种好处把人引向某个行动
senses.example: Bright packaging entices shoppers.
senses.exampleCN: 鲜艳的包装吸引购物者。
senses.why: The prefix en- puts a person into the state named by the old stem for urging or goading.
senses.whyCN: 前缀 en- 把人置于词干所指的被催促状态之中。

senses.title: To lead someone into something wrong
senses.definition: to persuade a person to act against their own interest or the rules
senses.definitionCN: 说服某人做违背自身利益或违反规则的事
senses.example: Peers enticed him into skipping school.
senses.exampleCN: 同伴怂恿他逃学。
senses.why: Because bait kills the animal it attracts, the verb readily carries a warning about the price of the offer.
senses.whyCN: 诱饵会害死被它吸引的动物，因此这个动词常带对代价的警告。

senses.title: To make something seem worth choosing
senses.definition: to make an offer, place, or job attractive enough to draw people
senses.definitionCN: 使某个提议、地方或工作足够诱人而招来参与者
senses.example: Tax breaks entice firms to invest.
senses.exampleCN: 税收优惠吸引企业投资。
senses.why: In commercial and policy writing the sense loses its blame and names simple attraction.
senses.whyCN: 在商业与政策写作中，这个义项不带责备，只表示单纯的吸引力。

intro.en: The verb pairs the prefix en- with a lost Old French stem of urging, first recorded in English in the fifteenth century.
intro.cn: 该动词以前缀 en- 加古法语中表催促的失传词干构成，英语最早记录于十五世纪。

items.en: In- supplies the prefix that French turned into en-.
items.cn: 拉丁语 in- 提供前缀，法语将其变为 en-。

items.en: Enticier means to stimulate or incite.
items.cn: 古法语 enticier 意为刺激、煽动。

items.en: The verb appears as entise in religious translation.
items.cn: 中古英语写作 entise，见于宗教译文。

items.en: Spelling settles, and the noun enticement is recorded.
items.cn: 近代早期拼法固定，名词 enticement 出现。

items.en: Commercial use softens the older sense of luring into harm.
items.cn: 现代商业用法淡化了引人受害的旧义。

note.en: Group one holds family forms and rhyming borrowings; group two holds other verbs of drawing people in.
note.cn: 第一组是同族形式与同尾借词；第二组是其他引人就范的动词。

entries.definition: The act or the bait itself, nominalised with the French ending.
entries.definitionCN: 指行为或诱饵本身，由法语名词词尾构成。

entries.definition: Used as an adjective for offers that look attractive.
entries.definitionCN: 作形容词，形容看起来诱人的报价。

entries.definition: Also from a Latin prefix plus a stem of moving, but it goads rather than baits.
entries.definitionCN: 同样来自前缀加推动词干，但指驱策而非给饵。

entries.definition: Shares the ending sound but not the history or the meaning.
entries.definitionCN: 只共享尾部读音，与来源和意义无关。

entries.definition: To draw away with temptation, with a stronger hint of danger.
entries.definitionCN: 以诱惑引开，危险意味更强。

entries.definition: To invite someone toward a wrong act, aimed at will rather than judgement.
entries.definitionCN: 邀请人做不该做的事，指向意志而非判断。

entries.definition: To persuade patiently with flattery or small favors, without bait.
entries.definitionCN: 用奉承或小恩耐心劝说，不设诱饵。

entries.definition: To offer a reward to change behaviour, neutral in tone.
entries.definitionCN: 以奖励改变行为，语气中性。

normalIntro.en: Entice sounds like nice plus en: something made appealing draws you in.
normalIntro.cn: entice 听感像 en 加 nice：被做得美好之物把你吸引过来。

normal.en: The pattern is entice somebody into or to do.
normal.cn: 句型是 entice somebody into 或 to do。

normal.en: Passive with by is common: enticed by promises.
normal.cn: 被动加 by 常见：被承诺吸引。

normal.en: Enticing is the friendly adjective; entice the verb keeps risk.
normal.cn: enticing 是友善的形容词，动词 entice 仍含风险。

normal.en: Markets use entice for customers; law uses it for corruption.
normal.cn: 市场语境用于招揽顾客，法律语境用于收买。

normal.en: The noun enticement can be the act or the object offered.
normal.cn: 名词 enticement 既可指行为，也可指所给的东西。

abstract.en: Picture a shiny seed placed just beyond the trap's edge.
abstract.cn: 想象一颗闪亮的种子放在陷阱边缘之外。

abstract.en: Imagine a neon sign above a doorway at night.
abstract.cn: 想象夜色里门口上方的霓虹灯牌。

abstract.en: Think of an open invitation card with a gift enclosed.
abstract.cn: 想想夹着礼物的空白请柬。

examples.en: The firm enticed engineers with equity shares.
examples.cn: 这家公司用股权吸引工程师。

examples.en: Nothing enticed her out of the house that evening.
examples.cn: 那晚没有什么能诱使她出门。

examples.en: Free credit enticed many first-time borrowers.
examples.cn: 免费额度诱使许多初次借款者上手。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「引他死」——音近 entice，引诱往往把人引向险境，所以是引诱；这只是拆词联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 in-（向内）→ 古法语 en- ＋ enticier（刺激、催促）→ 中古英语 entise → 现代英语 entice，核心义「用好处把人引进来」。

sensesIntro.en: The verb ranges from neutral attraction, through luring someone into harm, to commercial recruitment.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个动词从中性的吸引，经引人受害，延伸到商业上的招揽。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: bait set just out of reach so the target steps forward by itself.
core.cn: 核心意象：诱饵摆在刚好够不到之处，让对象自己走上前。

branches.en: Attraction by a visible benefit is the base sense.
branches.cn: 以可见好处吸引，是基础义项。

branches.en: When the benefit misleads, the verb becomes blaming.
branches.cn: 当好处误导人时，动词转为指责。

branches.en: Policy and commerce keep only the drawing power.
branches.cn: 政策与商业只保留招揽之力。

branches.en: Both explain why people choose to arrive.
branches.cn: 两者都解释人为何主动前来。

branches.en: The same offer can be a trap or simply a bargain.
branches.cn: 同一份好处既可能是陷阱，也可能只是划算。

intro.en: A French prefix plus a French stem, extended by English noun and adverb endings.
intro.cn: 法语前缀加法语词干，由英语名词与副词词尾扩展。

latinIntro.en: Latin In means into, and it is the scholarly source of the French prefix en-.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 in 表示向内，是法语前缀 en- 的书面来源。

items.exampleCN: en- 位于 entice 开头。

items.example: The stem survives only inside the verb.
items.exampleCN: 该词干只保留在这个动词里。
dis- 构成罕见动词 disentice。

definition_zh: 全部的；整个的；完整无缺的
definition_en: whole, with no part missing or left out
core_image: 一块布从一头铺到另一头，没有一处缺口
scene: 大雪下了整整一夜，第二天整个村子都白了。Snow fell all night, and the entire village was white by morning.
sceneCN: 这里 entire 是「整个的」（第 1 个义项：完整无缺的全部）；句意：雪下了一整夜，到早晨整个村子都白了。

pos.zh: 全部的；整个的；完整无缺的

senses.title: Whole, with nothing left out
senses.definition: including every part of something, with nothing missing
senses.definitionCN: 包含某物的每一部分，没有遗漏
senses.example: The entire class passed the test.
senses.exampleCN: 全班都通过了考试。
senses.why: The Latin root means untouched and whole, so the adjective names a thing with no part removed.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根意为「未被触碰、完整」，所以这个形容词指没有去掉任何部分的事物。

senses.title: Complete and unbroken
senses.definition: still in one piece, not damaged or divided
senses.definitionCN: 仍为一体，没有损坏或分裂
senses.example: The ancient wall is still entire after two thousand years.
senses.exampleCN: 两千年后，这堵古墙依然完整。
senses.why: The original sense of untouched survives in the idea of something whole and undamaged.
senses.whyCN: 「未被触碰」的原义，保留在「完整无损」这一含义中。

senses.title: Complete in degree
senses.definition: complete or total in an abstract sense, such as trust or agreement
senses.definitionCN: 在抽象意义上完全、彻底，如信任或一致
senses.example: He had the entire confidence of the board.
senses.exampleCN: 他拥有董事会的完全信任。
senses.why: Whole applied to abstract things means complete and unreserved.
senses.whyCN: 「整体」用于抽象事物，就表示完全、毫无保留。

intro.en: Entire comes from Latin integer, whole and untouched, from in-, not, and tangere, to touch, through Old French entier.
intro.cn: entire 来自拉丁语 integer（完整、未被触碰），由 in-（不）与 tangere（触碰）构成，经古法语 entier 进入英语。

items.en: Tangere means to touch or handle.
items.cn: tangere 意为触碰或接触。

items.en: In- here means not.
items.cn: 这里的 in- 表示「不」。

items.en: Integer means whole and untouched.
items.cn: integer 意为完整的、未被触碰的。

items.en: Entier keeps the sense of whole and complete.
items.cn: entier 保留「完整、完全」的意思。

items.en: Middle English entire describes something whole and sound.
items.cn: 中古英语 entire 描述完整而完好之物。

items.en: Modern English uses entire mainly for the whole of something.
items.cn: 现代英语中，entire 主要用于表示某事物的全部。

note.en: Entire is a wholeness word, and it sits near its family and near words for whole and complete.
note.cn: entire 是一个「完整」词，与自身词族以及表示全部和完整的词相邻。

entries.definition: completely
entries.definitionCN: 完全地

entries.definition: the state of being whole
entries.definitionCN: 整体；全部

entries.definition: to combine parts into a whole
entries.definitionCN: 整合；使成一体

entries.definition: complete, with no part missing
entries.definitionCN: 完整的；全部的

entries.definition: having all necessary parts
entries.definitionCN: 完整的；齐全的

entries.definition: including everything
entries.definitionCN: 全部的；总的

normalIntro.en: Entire comes from Latin integer, untouched or whole, so the word pictures something with no part removed.
normalIntro.cn: entire 来自拉丁语 integer（未被触碰、完整），所以这个词描绘没有去掉任何部分的事物。

normal.en: Integer means whole, and it also gives us the mathematical integer.
normal.cn: integer 意为完整，也给我们数学中的「整数」。

normal.en: The entire day means all of it, with nothing left out.
normal.cn: the entire day 指一整天，没有遗漏。

normal.en: The adverb entirely means completely.
normal.cn: 副词 entirely 表示完全地。

normal.en: The noun entirety appears in the phrase in its entirety.
normal.cn: 名词 entirety 出现在短语 in its entirety 中。

normal.en: Compare whole: whole is plainer, while entire is slightly more formal.
normal.cn: 对比 whole：whole 更朴素，entire 稍正式。

abstract.en: Picture a sheet of paper with no corner torn away.
abstract.cn: 想象一张纸没有任何一角被撕掉。

abstract.en: Imagine a circle closed without the smallest gap.
abstract.cn: 想象一个圆闭合得没有一丝缺口。

abstract.en: Think of a house lit from every window at once.
abstract.cn: 想象一座房子的每扇窗同时亮起。

examples.en: The entire class passed the test.
examples.cn: 全班都通过了考试。

examples.en: She read the entire report in one sitting.
examples.cn: 她一口气读完了整份报告。

examples.en: The entire village came to the wedding.
examples.cn: 全村人都来参加婚礼。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「in + tire」——一条轮胎也没有漏掉，就是完整无缺的全部；这只是拆词联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 in-（不）＋ tangere（触碰）→ integer（完整无缺的）→ 古法语 entier → 中古英语 entire，核心义「未被触碰、完整」。

sensesIntro.en: The word keeps the old sense of untouched wholeness, then extends it to physical completeness and finally to complete trust or agreement.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词保留「未被触碰的完整」这一古老含义，再扩展到物理上的完好，最后用于完全的信任或一致。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a whole sheet spread out with no corner missing.
core.cn: 核心意象：一整块布铺开，没有缺角。

branches.en: Including every part is the dominant modern sense.
branches.cn: 包含每一部分，是现代主要义项。

branches.en: Physical soundness keeps the original untouched idea.
branches.cn: 物理上的完好保留原初「未被触碰」的意思。

branches.en: Complete trust applies wholeness to abstract things.
branches.cn: 完全的信任把「整体」用于抽象事物。

branches.en: Something whole in quantity is often also whole in condition.
branches.cn: 数量上完整的东西，状况上往往也完好。

branches.en: The whole of a thing can be given completely or trusted fully.
branches.cn: 事物的整体可以被完整给出，也可以被完全信任。

intro.en: Entire is a Latin adjective reshaped by French, and its English family grows with -ly, -ty, and -ness.
intro.cn: entire 是经法语改造的拉丁形容词，英语词族由 -ly、-ty 与 -ness 扩展。

latinIntro.en: Latin integer means whole or untouched, from in-, not, and tangere, to touch.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 integer 意为完整或未被触碰，由 in-（不）与 tangere（触碰）构成。

items.exampleCN: in- 在 integer 中否定 tangere。

items.example: Tangere supplies the idea of touch.
Integer is the direct Latin source.
items.exampleCN: integer 是直接的拉丁语来源。

items.example: Entier carries the word into French.
items.exampleCN: entier 把这个词带入法语。
entirely 表示在每一部分上。

items.meaningCN: 表示状态或性质的词尾
表示状态或性质的词尾

items.example: Entireness is a rare synonym of entirety.
items.exampleCN: entireness 是 entirety 的罕见同义词。

definition_zh: 完全地；彻底地；仅仅
definition_en: completely, or only and nothing else
core_image: 一块布从头铺到尾，没有一寸遗漏
scene: 暴雨过后，整条山路都被泥水覆盖。After the storm, mud covered the mountain path entirely.
sceneCN: 这里 entirely 是「完全地」（第 1 个义项：在程度或范围上毫无遗漏）；句意：暴雨过后，泥水把山路完全盖住了。

senses.title: Completely, in every part
senses.definition: in every part or to the full degree, with nothing missing
senses.definitionCN: 在每一部分上或达到十足程度，没有任何遗漏
senses.example: I agree with you entirely.
senses.exampleCN: 我完全同意你。
senses.why: The adverb adds -ly to entire, so it describes something done in a whole and complete way.
senses.whyCN: 这个副词由 entire 加 -ly 构成，所以描述以完整、彻底的方式完成某事。

senses.title: Solely, and nothing else
senses.definition: used to say that something is only or wholly due to one thing
senses.definitionCN: 用于表示某事仅仅或完全由于某一原因
senses.example: The decision was entirely hers.
senses.exampleCN: 这个决定完全是她做的。
senses.why: If something is whole, nothing else is mixed in, so entirely can mean solely.
senses.whyCN: 如果某物是完整的，就没有别的东西掺入，因此 entirely 可以表示「仅仅」。

senses.title: Fully and without reservation
senses.definition: with complete commitment or agreement
senses.definitionCN: 带着完全的投入或赞同
senses.example: She trusted him entirely.
senses.exampleCN: 她完全信任他。
senses.why: Complete agreement leaves no room for doubt, which gives the sense of full-hearted trust.
senses.whyCN: 完全的赞同不留怀疑余地，于是产生「全心信任」的含义。

intro.en: Entirely is the adverb of entire, which comes from Latin integer, whole and untouched, through Old French entier.
intro.cn: entirely 是 entire 的副词形式；entire 来自拉丁语 integer（完整、未被触碰），经古法语 entier 进入英语。

items.en: Tangere means to touch or handle.
items.cn: tangere 意为触碰或接触。

items.en: In- here means not.
items.cn: 这里的 in- 表示「不」。

items.en: Integer means whole and untouched.
items.cn: integer 意为完整的、未被触碰的。

items.en: Entier keeps the sense of whole and complete.
items.cn: entier 保留「完整、完全」的意思。

items.en: Entire describes something whole and sound.
items.cn: 中古英语 entire 描述完整而完好之物。

items.en: The adverb entirely means completely or solely.
items.cn: 现代英语副词 entirely 表示完全地或仅仅。

note.en: Entirely belongs to the entire family and sits close to adverbs for complete degree.
note.cn: entirely 属于 entire 词族，并与表示完全程度的副词相邻。

entries.definition: whole, with no part missing
entries.definitionCN: 全部的；完整的

entries.definition: the state of being whole
entries.definitionCN: 整体；全部

entries.definition: completeness
entries.definitionCN: 完整性

entries.definition: in every way
entries.definitionCN: 完全地；彻底地

entries.definition: entirely, without exception
entries.definitionCN: 完全地；全部地

entries.definition: completely and only
entries.definitionCN: 完全地；纯粹地

normalIntro.en: Entirely is simply entire plus -ly: whatever is whole is done in a whole way.
normalIntro.cn: entirely 就是 entire 加 -ly：完整的东西，就以完整的方式去做。

normal.en: Entire means whole, so entirely means in a whole way.
normal.cn: entire 意为完整，所以 entirely 表示以完整的方式。

normal.en: Not entirely sure means not completely sure.
normal.cn: not entirely sure 就是不完全确定。

normal.en: The phrase entirely up to you means completely your choice.
normal.cn: 短语 entirely up to you 表示完全由你决定。

normal.en: Entirely can also mean solely, as in entirely her fault.
normal.cn: entirely 也可表示「仅仅」，如 entirely her fault。

normal.en: Compare partly, its opposite in degree.
normal.cn: 对比 partly，它是程度上的反义词。

abstract.en: Picture a blank sheet with no edge torn.
abstract.cn: 想象一张空白纸，边缘一处也没有撕破。

abstract.en: Imagine a lamp lighting every corner of one room.
abstract.cn: 想象一盏灯照亮一个房间的每个角落。

abstract.en: Think of a full glass filled to the very brim.
abstract.cn: 想象一只玻璃杯被倒到最满。

examples.en: The room was entirely empty when we arrived.
examples.cn: 我们到达时，房间完全是空的。

examples.en: Her answer was not entirely honest.
examples.cn: 她的回答并不完全诚实。

examples.en: The program is entirely free for students.
examples.cn: 这个项目对学生完全免费。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「in + tire」——轮胎一个都没落下，整辆车都齐全；这只是拆词联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 in-（不）＋ tangere（触碰）→ integer（完整无缺）→ 古法语 entier → entire ＋ -ly → entirely，核心义「完整地、完全地」。

sensesIntro.en: Entirely first means in every part, then narrows to solely, and finally describes full-hearted commitment.
sensesIntro.cn: entirely 先表示在每一部分上，再收窄为「仅仅」，最后描述毫无保留的投入。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a whole sheet spread out with no corner missing.
core.cn: 核心意象：一整块布铺开，没有缺角。

branches.en: Completeness in every part is the main adverbial sense.
branches.cn: 每一部分都完整，是主要副词义项。

branches.en: Wholeness with nothing mixed in gives the sense of solely.
branches.cn: 完整而没有别物掺入，产生「仅仅」的含义。

branches.en: Complete agreement extends the idea to full trust.
branches.cn: 完全的赞同把这一概念扩展到全心信任。

branches.en: Doing something completely often means doing it wholeheartedly.
branches.cn: 完全地做某事，往往意味着全身心投入。

branches.en: A decision made solely by one person can be trusted entirely.
branches.cn: 完全由一个人做出的决定，也可以被完全信任。

intro.en: Entirely is a Latin adjective reshaped by French, with the English adverb suffix -ly.
intro.cn: entirely 是经法语改造的拉丁形容词，加上英语副词词尾 -ly。

latinIntro.en: Latin integer means whole or untouched, from in-, not, and tangere, to touch.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 integer 意为完整或未被触碰，由 in-（不）与 tangere（触碰）构成。

items.exampleCN: in- 在 integer 中否定 tangere。

items.example: Tangere supplies the idea of touch.
Integer is the direct Latin source.
items.exampleCN: integer 是直接的拉丁语来源。

items.example: Entier carries the word into French.
items.exampleCN: entier 把这个词带入法语。
entirely 表示在每一部分上。

items.meaningCN: 表示状态或性质的词尾
表示状态或性质的词尾

items.example: Entireness is a rare synonym of entirety.
items.exampleCN: entireness 是 entirety 的罕见同义词。

definition_zh: 使有权；给予资格；给……命名
definition_en: to give someone a right, or to give a title to something
core_image: 一张写着名字的证件，让人有资格走进门内
scene: 公司规定，工作满一年的员工可以享受额外假期。The company entitles every worker with a year of service to extra holiday.
sceneCN: 这里 entitles 是 entitle 的第三人称单数，表示「使有权享受」（第 1 个义项：赋予某人权利或资格）；句意：公司让工作满一年的员工有权享受额外假期。

pos.zh: 使有权；给予资格；给……命名

senses.title: To give someone a right
senses.definition: to give a person the legal or moral right to have or do something
senses.definitionCN: 赋予某人拥有或做某事的法律或道义权利
senses.example: The law entitles citizens to free medical care.
senses.exampleCN: 法律使公民有权享受免费医疗。
senses.why: En- adds a sense of putting someone into a state, and title supplies the legal claim, so the verb means to grant a right.
senses.whyCN: 前缀 en- 表示使人进入某种状态，title 提供法律主张的含义，所以这个动词表示授予权利。

senses.title: To give a title to a work
senses.definition: to give a name or title to a book, film, song, or other work
senses.definitionCN: 给书、电影、歌曲或其他作品起名称
senses.example: The author entitled her first novel The Long Road.
senses.exampleCN: 作者把她的第一部小说命名为《长路》。
senses.why: Title also means the name of a work, so to entitle is to put a title on it.
senses.whyCN: title 也指作品的名称，因此 entitle 就是给作品加上标题。

senses.title: To give a name or label to a person
senses.definition: to give someone a particular name, label, or description
senses.definitionCN: 给某人一个特定的称呼、标签或描述
senses.example: Critics entitled him the voice of his generation.
senses.exampleCN: 评论家称他为那一代人的声音。
senses.why: A title can be an honor or a label, so the verb extends from naming works to naming people.
senses.whyCN: 称号既可以是荣誉也可以是标签，所以这个动词从给作品命名扩展到称呼人。

intro.en: Entitle comes from Latin titulus, a title or label, through Old French entitler, meaning to give a title to.
intro.cn: entitle 来自拉丁语 titulus（标题、称号），经古法语 entitler（给……加标题）进入英语。

items.en: Titulus means a title, label, or inscription.
items.cn: titulus 意为标题、标签或铭文。

items.en: Intitulare means to give a title to something.
items.cn: intitulare 意为给某物加上标题。

items.en: Entitler carries the legal and naming senses.
items.cn: entitler 同时带有法律与命名的含义。

items.en: Entitle means both to name and to give a claim.
items.cn: 中古英语 entitle 既表示命名，也表示赋予权利。

items.en: Modern English keeps the right sense in be entitled to.
items.cn: 现代英语在 be entitled to 中保留「有权」的含义。

note.en: Entitle is a giving word: it gives rights or names, so its company includes title words and words for granting.
note.cn: entitle 是一个「给予」词：给予权利或名称，所以它与 title 词族及表示授予的词相邻。

entries.definition: the name of a work or a rank
entries.definitionCN: 标题；称号

entries.definition: having a right or a title
entries.definitionCN: 有权的；有称号的

entries.definition: a right to have something
entries.definitionCN: 权利；应得的份额

entries.definition: to give official power or permission
entries.definitionCN: 授权；批准

entries.definition: to make someone eligible
entries.definitionCN: 使有资格

entries.definition: to give a name to something
entries.definitionCN: 命名；称呼

normalIntro.en: Entitle is en- plus title: to put someone or something into a title, whether a legal claim or a name.
normalIntro.cn: entitle 是 en- 加 title：把人或事物放进一个「名分」里，既可以是法律权利，也可以是名称。

normal.en: A ticket entitles you to a seat, and the verb entitles you to a right.
normal.cn: 一张票让你有座位，动词 entitle 让你有权利。

normal.en: Be entitled to means have the right to.
normal.cn: be entitled to 表示有权享有。

normal.en: A book is entitled, and so is a film.
normal.cn: 书可以被命名，电影也可以。

normal.en: The noun entitlement names the right itself.
normal.cn: 名词 entitlement 指权利本身。

normal.en: Compare title: title is the name, entitle is the act of giving it.
normal.cn: 对比 title：title 是名称，entitle 是给予名称的动作。

abstract.en: Picture a key being placed into a waiting hand.
abstract.cn: 想象一把钥匙被放进一双等待的手中。

abstract.en: Imagine a label being tied to a new book.
abstract.cn: 想象一个标签被系在一本新书上。

abstract.en: Think of a name written at the top of a page.
abstract.cn: 想象一个名字被写在页面顶端。

examples.en: This pass entitles you to enter the gallery.
examples.cn: 这张通行证使你有权进入画廊。

examples.en: She entitled her essay A Quiet Morning.
examples.cn: 她把自己的文章命名为《安静的早晨》。

examples.en: The ticket entitles each visitor to one free drink.
examples.cn: 这张票让每位参观者有权获得一杯免费饮料。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「en + title」——给你一个「头衔」，你就有资格；这只是拆词联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 titulus（标题、称号）→ 拉丁语 intitulare（加标题）→ 古法语 entitler → 中古英语 entitle，核心义「给予名分」，引申为赋予权利。

sensesIntro.en: Entitle moves from granting a legal claim to giving a work a title, and then to giving a person a label.
sensesIntro.cn: entitle 从授予法律权利，扩展到给作品加标题，再扩展到给人加称号。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a document with a name on it that opens a door.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张写有名字、可以打开一扇门的文书。

branches.en: Granting a right is the dominant legal sense.
branches.cn: 授予权利，是主要的法律义项。

branches.en: Giving a work its name keeps the original title idea.
branches.cn: 给作品命名，保留最初的「标题」概念。

branches.en: Giving a person a label extends naming to people.
branches.cn: 给人加称号，把命名扩展到人。

branches.en: Both rights and titles are things formally granted.
branches.cn: 权利与称号都是被正式授予的东西。

branches.en: A person can be legally entitled and publicly entitled.
branches.cn: 一个人可以依法有权，也可以被公开称呼。

intro.en: Entitle is built from en-, a Latin title word, and English endings for the derived forms.
intro.cn: entitle 由 en-、拉丁语 title 词根以及构成派生形式的英语词尾组成。

latinIntro.en: Latin titulus means a title or inscription, and intitulare means to give a title.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 titulus 意为标题或铭文，intitulare 意为加上标题。

items.example: En- puts a person into a titled state.
items.exampleCN: en- 把人带入拥有名分的状态。

items.example: Titulus is the root of the family.
items.exampleCN: titulus 是这个词族的词根。

items.example: Intitulare adds the Latin verb form.
items.exampleCN: intitulare 提供拉丁语动词形式。

items.example: Entitler brings the word into French.
items.exampleCN: entitler 把这个词带入法语。

items.meaning: to give a right or title
items.exampleCN: entitle 同时保留两种含义。

items.meaning: forming a past form or adjective
items.meaningCN: 构成过去式或形容词的词尾

items.example: Entitled describes someone with a claim.
items.exampleCN: entitled 描述拥有权利的人。

items.example: Title is the shorter noun beside the verb.
items.exampleCN: title 是与动词并存的较短名词。

definition_zh: 应享的权利；配额；应得感
definition_en: a right to have or receive something, the amount that is granted, or the belief that one deserves special treatment
core_image: 一份写明你名字的存单，凭它就能到柜台领走属于你的那份
scene: 政策规定每个家庭都有相应的补贴额度。Each family has an entitlement to a set allowance.
sceneCN: 这里 entitlement 是「应享的权利；配额」（第 1 个义项：依规可以获得的资格）；句意：每个家庭都有获得固定补贴的权利。

pos.zh: 应享的权利；配额；应得感

collocations.zh: 应得感；觉得自己理所当然该得到

derivatives.zh: 有资格的；自认为应得的

senses.title: A right to receive something
senses.definition: a situation in which a person may officially claim a benefit, service, or payment
senses.definitionCN: 个人可依规定领取福利、服务或报酬的情形
senses.example: Students have an entitlement to two tutorials weekly.
senses.exampleCN: 学生每周有权接受两次辅导。
senses.why: Built on entitle, which originally put a title or name on a document, so the noun is the right that the naming confers.
senses.whyCN: 该词造自 entitle，本指在文书上写明名分，因此名词指这名分所赋予的权利。

senses.title: The amount that is granted
senses.definition: the sum, leave, or benefit calculated as belonging to someone
senses.definitionCN: 经核算归属于某人的款项、假期或福利
senses.example: Her pension entitlement rose after the reform.
senses.exampleCN: 改革后她的养老金权益有所提高。
senses.why: Rights are counted in policy offices, so the word shifts from the claim to the figure attached to it.
senses.whyCN: 政策部门需要清点权利，于是词义从资格转向其对应的数字。

senses.title: An expected claim on others' attention
senses.definition: the attitude of believing that one deserves privileges without earning them
senses.definitionCN: 认为无需付出就理应享有特权的心理态度
senses.example: A sense of entitlement made the intern difficult.
senses.exampleCN: 强烈的应得感让这名实习生难以相处。
senses.why: Used psychologically, the noun describes a felt entitlement rather than a legally granted one.
senses.whyCN: 用于心理层面时，这个名词指主观感受到的应得，而非法律授予的权利。

intro.en: The noun sits on entitle, whose stem title comes from Latin titulus, a label or placard.
intro.cn: 该名词立于 entitle 之上，其词干 title 来自拉丁语 titulus，指标签或牌示。

items.en: Titulus means a placard or inscription.
items.cn: titulus 指牌示或题铭。

items.en: Titre gives English the word title.
items.cn: titre 为英语提供 title。

items.en: Entitle is used for giving a book its name.
items.cn: entitle 早期用于给书命题。

items.en: Legal writing uses entitle for conferring a claim.
items.cn: 十九世纪法律文体用以表示赋予请求权。

items.en: Welfare states create entitlement as a policy noun.
items.cn: 二十世纪福利国家把它变成政策名词。

items.en: Psychology adopts the phrase sense of entitlement.
items.cn: 现代英语中心理学采纳应得感这一说法。

note.en: Group one holds the verb family and the parallel nominal builds; group two holds other words for a claim.
note.cn: 第一组是动词同族与同类构词；第二组是其他表示应得资格的词。

entries.definition: The source verb, which also means to give a work its name.
entries.definitionCN: 源动词，另有为作品命题之义。

entries.definition: Marked as having a right, or, critically, behaving as if one does.
entries.definitionCN: 有资格的；若含批评语气则指自认为理所当然。

entries.definition: Built with the same French ending but from a different stem.
entries.definitionCN: 词尾相同而词干不同。

entries.definition: Sounds close and shares the ending, but names an achievement reached.
entries.definitionCN: 读音相近、词尾相同，指已达到的成就。

entries.definition: The broadest word for what belongs to a person by law or fairness.
entries.definitionCN: 指法律或公平归属某人的最通用词。

entries.definition: An advantage held by some and not all, often unearned.
entries.definitionCN: 部分人而非所有人享有的好处，常非挣得。

entries.definition: What is properly owed, used for payments and leave.
entries.definitionCN: 应付款项或应休假期。

entries.definition: A fixed amount given officially, close to the policy sense.
entries.definitionCN: 官方给出的固定数额，接近政策义。

normalIntro.en: Entitlement is entitle plus ment, so it is the state of being named as having a claim.
normalIntro.cn: entitlement 是 entitle 加 ment，因此指被写明拥有请求权的状态。

normal.en: Say entitlement to something, never entitlement for doing.
normal.cn: 搭配为 entitlement to something，不说 entitlement for doing。

normal.en: In policy texts the plural entitlements means counted benefits.
normal.cn: 政策文本中复数 entitlements 指经核算的多项福利。

normal.en: The phrase sense of entitlement is the psychology use.
normal.cn: 短语 sense of entitlement 属心理学用法。

normal.en: Do not read it as political power; it is a claim to receive.
normal.cn: 不要译作权力，它指领取的资格。

normal.en: Compare entitled, which can flatter or accuse depending on tone.
normal.cn: 对比 entitled，依语气可褒可贬。

abstract.en: Picture a card with your name printed on it and a figure beside the name.
abstract.cn: 想象一张印有你姓名与旁边数字的卡片。

abstract.en: Imagine a queue in which one person acts as if served before arriving.
abstract.cn: 想象一人未到场却理所当然被先服务的队伍。

abstract.en: Think of a ledger page headed with your own title.
abstract.cn: 想想抬头写着你的名分的那页账簿。

examples.en: The reform changed pension entitlements for teachers.
examples.cn: 改革改变了教师的养老金权益。

examples.en: Every child has an entitlement to schooling.
examples.cn: 每个孩子都享有受教育的权利。

examples.en: Staff questioned the entitlement to extra leave days.
examples.cn: 员工对额外休假的资格提出疑问。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「印抬头铭」——把名字印在抬头，所以 entitlement 是应享的权利；这只是拆词联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 titulus（牌示）→ 古法语 titre → 英语 title＋en- 构成 entitle → entitle＋名词词尾 -ment → entitlement，核心义「被写明归属于你的资格」。

sensesIntro.en: The noun moves from an official claim, to the amount attached to it, to a personality trait of expecting privileges.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个名词从官方资格，走向其对应数额，再指向一种期待特权的性格特征。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a written grant with your name on it that you can present and collect.
core.cn: 核心意象：一份写着你名字的授予文书，可出示并领取。

branches.en: The official claim is the organising sense.
branches.cn: 官方资格是组织性义项。

branches.en: Counted benefits turn the claim into figures.
branches.cn: 核算后的福利把资格变成数字。

branches.en: Psychology names the feeling without the document.
branches.cn: 心理学指称这种感受本身，并无文书。

branches.en: Both belong to administration and rules.
branches.cn: 两者同属行政与规则领域。

branches.en: Generous grants can feed an attitude of deserving.
branches.cn: 优厚的授予可能滋养应得心态。

intro.en: The word stacks a prefix, a Latin noun stem, and two layers of nominal endings.
intro.cn: 这个词叠加前缀、拉丁名词词干与两层名词词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin Titulus means a placard, and inscribere means to write upon a surface.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 titulus 指牌示，inscribere 指在表面书写。

items.exampleCN: en- 位于 entitle 开头。

items.meaning: to give a right or a name

definition_zh: 实体；独立存在物；单位
definition_en: something that exists independently as a distinct unit, especially an organisation or a being
core_image: 黑夜的房间里只有一盏灯，那个轮廓清晰的东西独立于周围一切而存在
scene: 分公司在法律上是一个独立单位。The branch is a separate legal entity.
sceneCN: 这里 entity 是「实体；独立单位」（第 2 个义项：法律上可单独承担责任的存在）；句意：这家分公司是独立的法律实体。

derivatives.zh: 无足轻重的人；不存在之物

senses.title: Anything that exists on its own
senses.definition: a thing that has its own existence, separate from other things
senses.definitionCN: 独立于他物而自身存在的事物
senses.example: A forest is more than a collection of trees; it is an entity.
senses.exampleCN: 森林不只是树木的集合，它是一个实体。
senses.why: The word is built on the Latin participle for being, so its first job is to name something that is.
senses.whyCN: 这个词建立在拉丁语「存在」的分词之上，因此首要功能是命名那个存在着的东西。

senses.title: An organisation treated as one unit
senses.definition: a company, fund, or institution that holds rights and duties in its own name
senses.definitionCN: 以自身名义持有权利与义务的公司、基金或机构
senses.example: The two firms merged into a single entity.
senses.exampleCN: 这两家公司合并为一个实体。
senses.why: Law needs a single addressable being behind paperwork, so the philosophical word becomes administrative.
senses.whyCN: 法律需要在文书背后有一个可指称的统一存在，于是哲学术语转为行政用语。

senses.title: A being of uncertain or invented nature
senses.definition: a being that is felt to exist although it cannot be identified, as in fiction or belief
senses.definitionCN: 被认为存在却无法指认的存在体，常见于小说或信仰
senses.example: The story describes an entity that lives in the deep water.
senses.exampleCN: 小说描述了一种栖身深水的存在。
senses.why: Applied to beings whose existence is only asserted, the noun keeps its core idea and loses its evidence.
senses.whyCN: 用于仅被宣称存在的生灵时，这个名词保留核心义而失去证据。

intro.en: Entity grew out of Medieval Latin entitas, formed from the Latin participle ens, being.
intro.cn: entity 源自中古拉丁语 entitas，由拉丁语分词 ens（存在者）构成。

items.en: Esse means to be, and its participle ens names a being.
items.cn: esse 意为存在，其分词 ens 指存在者。

items.en: Entitas was coined by scholastic writers to discuss being itself.
items.cn: 经院作者造出 entitas 以讨论存在本身。

items.en: Entité supplies the English shape.
items.cn: entité 为英语提供词形。

items.en: Entity enters philosophy and law writing.
items.cn: 近代早期英语中该词进入哲学与法律写作。

items.en: Commercial usage applies it to companies as units.
items.cn: 十九世纪商业用法把它用于公司单位。

items.en: Computing borrows the term for recorded objects.
items.cn: 现代英语中计算领域借用该词指被记录的对象。

note.en: Group one holds words sharing the being stem or the ending; group two holds other unit words.
note.cn: 第一组是同词干或同词尾的词；第二组是其他表示单位的词。

entries.definition: A person or thing so slight that it hardly counts as existing.
entries.definitionCN: 轻渺到近乎不存在的个人或事物。

entries.definition: Shares the abstract ending but comes from identical rather than being.
entries.definitionCN: 词尾相同，却出自 identical 而非存在。

entries.definition: Relating to entity or to existence as such.
entries.definitionCN: 关于实体的，或关于存在本身的。

entries.definition: Another Latin abstract in -ity, but it names a property, not a being.
entries.definitionCN: 同为 -ity 结尾的拉丁抽象名词，指属性而非存在者。

entries.definition: The plain English equivalent for whatever exists.
entries.definitionCN: 指一切存在者的通俗对应词。

entries.definition: One member of a set, used in administration and measurement.
entries.definitionCN: 集合中的一个成员，用于行政与计量。

entries.definition: A planned body of people, broader than the legal notion.
entries.definitionCN: 有组织的人群整体，宽于法律概念。

entries.definition: In law, any holder of rights, including a company.
entries.definitionCN: 法律上指权利持有者，公司也包括在内。

normalIntro.en: Entity is tied to the Latin verb to be, so keep existence as the anchor.
normalIntro.cn: entity 与拉丁语「存在」动词相连，因此始终以存在为锚点。

normal.en: Legal entity is the fixed phrase for a company that can sue and be sued.
normal.cn: 法人实体是法律上可起诉与被诉公司的固定说法。

normal.en: Entities is countable, so write two entities, not two entity.
normal.cn: 可数名词，two entities 而非 two entity。

normal.en: In fiction the word hints at a being nobody can name.
normal.cn: 小说中该词暗示无人能指认的存在。

normal.en: Databases use entity for a stored object type.
normal.cn: 数据库用 entity 指存储的对象类型。

normal.en: Do not swap it with integrity, which concerns wholeness and honesty.
normal.cn: 不要与 integrity 混用，后者指完整与正直。

abstract.en: Picture one lit window in a long dark row of houses.
abstract.cn: 想象长长一列暗屋中唯一亮着的一扇窗。

abstract.en: Imagine a stamp placed on a folder to mark it as separate.
abstract.cn: 想象档案夹上盖下的一枚独立印章。

abstract.en: Think of a footprint that belongs to no known animal.
abstract.cn: 想想不属于任何已知动物的脚印。

examples.en: The fund operates as a distinct legal entity.
examples.cn: 该基金作为独立的法律实体运作。

examples.en: Small entities were exempt from the new reporting duty.
examples.cn: 小型实体可免于新的申报义务。

examples.en: Writers often invent an entity that cannot be seen.
examples.cn: 作家常虚构一个看不见的存在。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「按梯」——按着梯子一层层独立存在，所以 entity 是实体；这只是拆词联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 esse（存在）的分词 ens／ent-＋抽象名词词尾 -itas → 中古拉丁语 entitas → 法语 entité → 英语 entity，核心义「自身存在着的东西」。

sensesIntro.en: The noun begins in philosophy as whatever exists, becomes an administrative unit, and ends as a name for unverifiable beings.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个名词起于哲学中的一切存在者，转为行政单位，最后成为无法证实之存在的称呼。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one outline standing apart from everything around it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个轮廓独立于周遭万物而立。

branches.en: Existence itself is the philosophical root sense.
branches.cn: 存在本身是哲学的根源义项。

branches.en: Law draws a boundary and attaches rights to it.
branches.cn: 法律画出边界并在其上附着权利。

branches.en: Belief keeps the shape while dropping the proof.
branches.cn: 信仰保留形态却去掉证据。

branches.en: Both name something only asserted to exist.
branches.cn: 两者都命名仅被宣称存在之物。

branches.en: Both treat the thing as one addressable whole.
branches.cn: 两者都把对象视为可指称的整体。

intro.en: A Latin participle stem joins an abstract ending and gains modern legal and technical senses.
intro.cn: 拉丁分词词干加抽象词尾，并衍生出现代法律与技术义项。

latinIntro.en: Latin Esse means to be, ens means being, and entia means the things that are.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 esse 表存在，ens 表存在者，entia 表诸存在之物。

items.example: Ent- carries the idea of existence.
The adjective is rare and technical.

items.exampleCN: 法律用法固定了这个义项。

items.example: Plural changes the ending from y to ies.
items.exampleCN: 复数把词尾 y 变为 ies。
esse 是整个词族的基础。
